raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary
- Resolves the merge conflict blocking https://github.com/AMD-AGI/TraceLens/pull/1071 against current `main`.
- Keeps this branch's op-projection perf metrics (`compute_perf_metrics` no longer takes `non_data_mov`, `python_path`, or `enable_origami`).
- Keeps `compute_roofline_time_and_bound` from `main`, which the model-explorer roofline still calls.
- Drops the coverage omit for `run_perf_model.py`, which this branch removes, and drops `python_path` from the perf models `main` added so they match the base constructors.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/Visualizer/test_roofline_projection.py`
- [x] `tests/test_op_projections.py`
- [x] `tests/test_treeperf.py -k compute_roofline_time_and_bound`
- [ ] Confirm GitHub reports PR #1071 as mergeable after this lands on `ajassani/specialized-perf-model`


Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

         run: |
           python -m pip install --upgrade pip coverage

-          python -m coverage xml
-          python -m coverage report --fail-under=95
+          # A skipped suite leaves its package at 0% and pulls the 95% gate
+          # down. coverage.py keeps a single --omit value, so a second flag
+          # replaces the first and that package stays in the total. Pass every
+          # skipped package in one comma-separated value, and quote it so the
+          # shell does not expand the globs. A push runs both suites and
+          # passes no flag.
+          OMIT=""
+          if [ "$MODELUTILS" != "true" ]; then
+            OMIT="TraceLens/ModelUtils/*"
+          fi
+          if [ "$VISUALIZER" != "true" ]; then
+            if [ -n "$OMIT" ]; then
+              OMIT="$OMIT,TraceLens/Visualizer/*"
+            else
+              OMIT="TraceLens/Visualizer/*"
+            fi
+          fi
+          if [ -n "$OMIT" ]; then
+            python -m coverage xml --omit="$OMIT"
+            python -m coverage report --fail-under=95 --omit="$OMIT"
+          else
+            python -m coverage xml
+            python -m coverage report --fail-under=95
+          fi
 
       - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
         if: success() && needs.select-pr-tests.outputs.mode == 'all'

+---
+name: roofline-augment-agent
+description: Derive the checkpoint, parallelism, and per-phase batch/sequence arguments for the analytical roofline augmentation from orchestrator artifacts. Invoked by the orchestrator only when analytical roofline augmentation is enabled.
+model: claude-opus-4-7-high
+---
+
+# Roofline Augment Subagent
+
+Derive the arguments for `roofline_augment` from artifacts already on disk. You do not compute a roofline and you do not edit findings. The orchestrator runs the projection script on the file you write.
+
+Use a value only when one of the sources below states it. When a required field cannot be derived, write `null` and set `skipped` to `"Cannot be inferred from trace"`. Do not guess, and do not use a CLI default (batch 1, sequence 2048, tp 1 on a multi-rank trace) as if it had been measured.
+
+---
+
+## Context Passing
+
+**Required context provided by orchestrator:**
+- `output_dir`: base analysis output directory
+- `platform`: platform name from Step 0 (for example `MI300X`)
+- `prefix`: command prefix from `<output_dir>/cache/cmd_prefix.txt` — substitute the command for `{CMD}`
+
+**Inputs:**
+- `<output_dir>/metadata/model_info.json` — `model`, `architecture`, `scale`, `precision`
+- `<output_dir>/metadata/condensed_op_info.csv` — columns `name`, `Input type`, `Input Dims`. If the file is missing, produce it and then read it:
+
+```bash
+<prefix> python3 -c "
+import sys
+from TraceLens.Agent.Analysis.utils.report_utils import prepare_model_identification_data
+if not prepare_model_identification_data('<output_dir>'):
+    sys.exit(1)
+"
+```
+
+- `<output_dir>/metadata/nn_modules.txt` — nn.Module class names, when present
+- `<output_dir>/cache/run_config.yaml` — `analysis_mode`, and each job's `name` and `phase`
+- `<output_dir>/category_data/category_manifest.json` — `focus_csv_dir`, and `gpu_utilization.jobs` (each entry has a `phase`)
+- The perf CSVs in `focus_csv_dir` (or `<output_dir>/perf_report_csvs` when the manifest has no `focus_csv_dir`). Read headers and the rows you need; do not load a trace JSON.
+
+**Output file you must write:**
+- `<output_dir>/metadata/roofline_augment_args.json`
+
+---
+
+## Output Schema
+
+```json
+{
+  "source": "<hf-id-or-checkpoint-dir or null>",
+  "code_path": null,
+  "engine": "vllm",
+  "tp": 8,
+  "pp": 1,
+  "ep": 1,
+  "gpu_arch_name": "<platform>",
+  "phases": [
+    {"phase": "prefill", "batch_size": 1, "seq_len": 8192, "dims": {}},
+    {"phase": "decode", "batch_size": 32, "seq_len": 1, "dims": {"past_len": 65536}}
+  ],
+  "skipped": null
+}
+```
+
+`engine` is `vllm`, `sglang`, or `null`. `phases` is a list; each `phase` is `prefill` or `decode`. `dims` is an object of integer shape overrides (`past_len` for decode). `skipped` is `null` when `source` and `phases` are both resolved, and `"Cannot be inferred from trace"` otherwise. On the unresolved path set `source` to `null` and `phases` to `[]`.
+
+---
+
+## Derivation
+
+### source
+
+Read `model` from `metadata/model_info.json`.
+
+- Use it as `source` when it is a Hugging Face id: exactly one `/`, no spaces, both sides non-empty (`org/name`).
+- Use it as `source` when it is an absolute path to a directory that contains `config.json`.
+- Otherwise `source` is `null`. A family name (`LLM`, `Inkling`, `Workload`) is not a checkpoint. Do not invent an id from `nn_modules.txt`.
+
+`code_path` stays `null` unless that same evidence is an existing modeling `.py` file.
+
+### engine
+
+Read `analysis_mode` from `cache/run_config.yaml`. Set `engine` only when `analysis_mode` is `inference`:
+
+- `vllm` when `nn_modules.txt` or `condensed_op_info.csv` `name` cells contain `vllm`
+- `sglang` when they contain `sglang`
+
+Leave `engine` `null` otherwise. Do not set it from the platform.
+
+### gpu_arch_name
+
+Copy `<platform>` from the orchestrator context. Do not search for an arch file.
+
+### tp, pp, ep
+
+Look for an explicit degree, in this order:
+
+1. A key `tp` / `tensor_parallel_size`, `pp` / `pipeline_parallel_size`, or `ep` / `expert_parallel_size` in `cache/run_config.yaml` or in a perf-CSV column of that name. Use the integer you find, and `1` for an axis that is absent.
+2. Otherwise, if every perf CSV that has a `rank` column contains a single distinct rank, use `tp=1`, `pp=1`, `ep=1`.
+3. Otherwise the split of a multi-rank trace is not in the file. Set `tp`, `pp`, and `ep` to `null`, `phases` to `[]`, and `skipped` to `"Cannot be inferred from trace"`. Do not divide a world size into tp, pp, and ep.
+
+### phases
+
+Collect candidate phase names from `cache/run_config.yaml` `jobs[].phase` and from `category_manifest.json` `gpu_utilization.jobs.*.phase`. Keep `prefill` and `decode` only (case-insensitive; write them in lowercase). A job phase with any other name is not a roofline phase.
+
+For each kept phase, read `batch_size` and `seq_len` from `condensed_op_info.csv` `Input Dims` on attention-like ops (`attention`, `sdpa`, `bmm` with a 4D shape):
+
+- The leading dimension of a `[B, ...]`, `[B, S, ...]`, or `[B, H, S, D]` shape is `batch_size`.
+- **prefill:** `seq_len` is the sequence axis (the axis that is not a head count and is greater than 1). Leave `dims` empty.
+- **decode:** `seq_len` is `1` when the query length is 1. Put the cached context length in `dims.past_len`.
+
+When a trace has no job phase, infer the phase from those shapes: query length `1` with a cached context is `decode`; a query length equal to the context is `prefill`. When both patterns occur, emit both phases.
+
+When `Input Dims` is empty for every op that could supply `batch_size` and `seq_len` for a phase, drop that phase. When no phase remains, set `phases` to `[]` and `skipped` to `"Cannot be inferred from trace"`. Do not fill in batch `1` or sequence `2048`.
+
+A `multi_trace` run projects each resolved phase once. Do not collapse prefill and decode into one phase.
+
+---
+
+## Error Handling
+
+- If `model_info.json` is missing or `source` cannot be resolved, still write the file with `source: null`, `phases: []`, and `skipped: "Cannot be inferred from trace"`.
+- Always leave `metadata/roofline_augment_args.json` in place before returning. Do not write `priority_data.json` or `roofline_augmentation.json`.

+# ===========================================================================
+# Semantic-analysis artifact validators
+#
+# The semantic-comparison path (skills/analysis-orchestrator/agents/) has three
+# LLM-authored JSON artifacts. Each validator does a schema check plus a
+# referential check against the context the agent was given, and returns
+# (passed, errors) so the orchestrator can use it as a retry gate before the
+# corresponding apply step rewrites semantic_block.
+# ===========================================================================
+

+def _marker_attrs(text, kind):
+    """Yield (match, attrs) for each ``kind`` impact marker in ``text``."""
+    for m in MarkerValidator.BEGIN_RE.finditer(text):
+        attrs = dict(MarkerValidator.ATTR_RE.findall(m.group(1)))
+        if attrs.get("kind") == kind:
+            yield m, attrs
+
+
+def _load_json_for_validation(path):
+    """Load a JSON file for validation; return (doc, errors)."""
+    if not os.path.exists(path):
+        return None, [f"File not found: {path}"]
+    try:
+        with open(path) as f:
+            return json.load(f), []
+    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as e:
+        return None, [f"Could not parse {path}: {e}"]
+
+
+def _missing_backrefs(replacement, rx):
+    """Group references in a re.sub replacement that the pattern can't satisfy.
+
+    Catches the failure that ``re`` only raises at substitution time (a
+    backreference with no matching capture group), which ``stem_for`` silently
+    swallows at runtime. Returns the set of offending references.
+    """
+    bad = set()
+    for m in re.finditer(r"\\(\d+)|\\g<([^>]*)>", replacement):
+        num, name = m.group(1), m.group(2)
+        if num is not None:
+            if int(num) > rx.groups:
+                bad.add(num)
+        elif name is not None:
+            if name.isdigit():
+                if int(name) > rx.groups:
+                    bad.add(name)
+            elif name not in rx.groupindex:
+                bad.add(name)
+    return bad
+

+def validate_stem_rules(rules_path):
+    """Validate a kernel-stem-preprocessing ``stem_rules.json``.
+
+    Schema: ``{"rules": [...]}`` (or a bare list); each rule a dict with a
+    compilable ``pattern``, ``action`` in collapse/preserve/drop, a string
+    ``replacement`` and a non-empty ``note``. Referential: a ``collapse``
+    replacement may only reference capture groups the pattern defines, and
+    duplicate patterns are flagged (first match wins, so a later duplicate is
+    dead).
+
+    Returns:
+        (passed: bool, errors: list[str])
+    """
+    doc, errors = _load_json_for_validation(rules_path)
+    if errors:
+        return False, errors
+
+    rules = doc.get("rules") if isinstance(doc, dict) else doc
+    if not isinstance(rules, list):
+        return False, ["Top-level must be a list or an object with a 'rules' list."]
+
+    seen_patterns = {}
+    for i, r in enumerate(rules):
+        if not isinstance(r, dict):
+            errors.append(f"rule {i}: must be an object")
+            continue
+
+        action = r.get("action", "collapse")
+        if action not in ("collapse", "preserve", "drop"):
+            errors.append(
+                f"rule {i}: invalid action {action!r} (collapse/preserve/drop)"
+            )
+
+        pattern = r.get("pattern")
+        rx = None
+        if not isinstance(pattern, str) or pattern == "":
+            errors.append(f"rule {i}: 'pattern' must be a non-empty string")
+        else:
+            try:
+                rx = re.compile(pattern)
+            except re.error as e:
+                errors.append(f"rule {i}: bad regex {pattern!r}: {e}")
+            else:
+                if pattern in seen_patterns:
+                    errors.append(
+                        f"rule {i}: duplicate pattern {pattern!r} (rule "
+                        f"{seen_patterns[pattern]} matches first; this one is dead)"
+                    )
+                else:
+                    seen_patterns[pattern] = i
+
+        note = r.get("note")
+        if not isinstance(note, str) or not note.strip():
+            errors.append(f"rule {i}: 'note' is required (non-empty rationale)")
+
+        replacement = r.get("replacement", "")
+        if not isinstance(replacement, str):
+            errors.append(f"rule {i}: 'replacement' must be a string")
+        elif action == "collapse" and rx is not None:
+            bad = _missing_backrefs(replacement, rx)
+            if bad:
+                errors.append(
+                    f"rule {i}: replacement {replacement!r} references missing "
+                    f"group(s) {sorted(bad)} (pattern defines {rx.groups})"
+                )
+
+    return (not errors), errors
+

+        for i, r in enumerate(entries):
+            if not isinstance(r, dict):
+                errors.append(f"{key}[{i}]: must be an object")
+                continue
+            rid = r.get("id", r.get(side))
+            if rid not in ids:
+                errors.append(f"{key}[{i}]: id {rid!r} not in only_in_{nm}")
+            lbl = r.get("label")
+            if not isinstance(lbl, str) or not lbl.strip():
+                errors.append(f"{key}[{i}]: 'label' must be a non-empty string")
+
+    return (not errors), errors
+
+
+def validate_kernel_coherence_decisions(decisions_path, context_path):
+    """Validate a kernel-coherence ``kernel_coherence_decisions.json``.
+
+    Schema: ``context_renames`` / ``fallback_remap_a`` / ``fallback_remap_b`` /
+    ``fallback_remap_regex_a`` / ``fallback_remap_regex_b`` are string->string
+    maps with non-empty values; ``notes`` optional string. Referential (against
+    ``kernel_coherence_context.json``): ``context_renames`` keys are
+    ``context_catalog`` ids, ``fallback_remap_*`` keys are symbols from the
+    matching ``one_sided_in_*`` list, and every ``fallback_remap_regex_*`` key
+    compiles as a regex.
+
+    Returns:
+        (passed: bool, errors: list[str])
+    """
+    decisions, errors = _load_json_for_validation(decisions_path)
+    if errors:
+        return False, errors
+    context, errors = _load_json_for_validation(context_path)
+    if errors:
+        return False, errors
+
+    errors = []
+    catalog_ids = {
+        e.get("id") for e in context.get("context_catalog", []) if isinstance(e, dict)
+    }
+    one_sided = {
+        "a": set(context.get("one_sided_in_a", [])),
+        "b": set(context.get("one_sided_in_b", [])),
+    }
+
+    def _check_str_map(obj, key):
+        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
+            errors.append(f"'{key}' must be an object")
+            return {}
+        for k, v in obj.items():
+            if not isinstance(v, str) or not v.strip():
+                errors.append(f"{key}[{k!r}]: value must be a non-empty string")
+        return obj
+
+    renames = _check_str_map(
+        decisions.get("context_renames", {}) or {}, "context_renames"
+    )
+    for k in renames:
+        if k not in catalog_ids:
+            errors.append(f"context_renames: id {k!r} not in context_catalog")
+
+    for side in ("a", "b"):
+        key = f"fallback_remap_{side}"
+        fr = _check_str_map(decisions.get(key, {}) or {}, key)
+        for k in fr:
+            if k not in one_sided[side]:
+                errors.append(f"{key}: symbol {k!r} not in one_sided_in_{side}")
+
+        rkey = f"fallback_remap_regex_{side}"
+        rr = _check_str_map(decisions.get(rkey, {}) or {}, rkey)
+        for k in rr:
+            try:
+                re.compile(k)
+            except re.error as e:
+                errors.append(f"{rkey}: bad regex {k!r}: {e}")
+
+    notes = decisions.get("notes")
+    if notes is not None and not isinstance(notes, str):
+        errors.append("'notes' must be a string")
+
+    return (not errors), errors

+# TraceLens Agent: Model Visualizer
+
+The model visualizer agent exports a Hugging Face checkpoint, a local checkpoint directory, or a whitelisted modeling repo to an interactive [Model Explorer](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/model-explorer) graph. A skill drives the `visualize_model_in_explorer` CLI: install check, one export command, then a check that the HTML or JSON file is real. The export is static analysis of `modeling_*.py` plus a meta-device shape pass. It runs on CPU and does not load checkpoint weights.
+
+The tool itself is documented in [TraceLens/Visualizer/README.md](../../Visualizer/README.md).
+
+This package also ships the [model-roofline-projection](skills/model-roofline-projection/SKILL.md) skill, which drives `TraceLens_model_roofline_projection` to project a kernel-by-kernel roofline from the same checkpoint and modeling source, with no trace and no GPU run. See [docs/how-to/generate-model-roofline-projection.md](../../../docs/how-to/generate-model-roofline-projection.md) for that tool.
+
+---
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+### 1. Install TraceLens with the Visualizer extra
+
+Installing the package ships this skill under `TraceLens/Agent/Visualizer/skills/model-visualizer/`. The exporter is the `[Visualizer]` extra.
+
+**Local checkout:**
+
+```bash
+pip install -e ".[Visualizer]"
+```
+
+**From GitHub:**
+
+```bash
+pip install "TraceLens[Visualizer] @ git+https://github.com/AMD-AGI/TraceLens.git"
+```
+
+Python 3.10 or newer. No GPU, ROCm, or CUDA wheel is required. A gated checkpoint needs `HF_TOKEN`.
+
+### 2. Model source
+
+One of:
+
+- a Hugging Face model id (`org/model`)
+- a local directory that contains `config.json`
+- a GitHub modeling repo that is already allowlisted, or passed with `--allow-repo`
+
+Network is required the first time a Hub model or an unpkg viewer asset is fetched. Cached checkpoints export offline.
+
+---
+
+## Quick Start - How to Use
+
+> **Note**: The skill is portable across agentic runners that discover skill files (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex). The instructions below use the Cursor IDE and the `agent` CLI.
+
+> **Skill path in the package:** `TraceLens/Agent/Visualizer/skills/model-visualizer/` (`SKILL.md`, `reference.md`, `skill-card.md`). Cursor project discovery reads `.cursor/skills/`; symlink or copy this folder there for automatic pickup.
+
+### To run via chat
+
+1. **Invoke:**
+
+   ```text
+   Follow the model visualizer installed with TraceLens and export <model> to <path>.html
+   ```
+
+2. **Provide if prompted:**
+   - Hugging Face id or local checkpoint path
+   - HTML path, or a request to serve the graph locally
+   - Runtime regime when it is not a cold rectangular prefill (packed layout, decode, warm cache, training)
+   - Attention implementation when it should not follow the checkpoint (`eager`, `sdpa`, `flash_attention_2`, `flash_attention_3`, or another `_attn_implementation` string)
+   - Config overrides as `KEY=VALUE` (repeatable; dotted keys reach nested configs)
+   - Sharding source and counts: Hugging Face plans by default, or `--engine vllm` / `--engine sglang`, with `--tp`, `--pp`, and `--ep`
+
+3. **Results:**
+   - **Primary output:** a self-contained `.html` file. Open it in a browser. The visualizer element loads from unpkg on first open.
+   - **Several GPU groups:** `<stem>_subgraph_<i>.html` next to that file.
+   - **Optional:** a Model Explorer JSON payload (`-o model.json`) and a flat operator JSON (`--operators-json`).
+
+### To run headless
+
+Install the Cursor CLI if you want a non-interactive run:
+
+```bash
+curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash
+```
+
+Pass the model and the output path in the prompt so the skill does not ask questions:
+
+```bash
+agent --model claude-opus-4-8-thinking-medium --print --force --trust \
+    "Follow the model visualizer installed with the TraceLens pip package (look under TraceLens/Agent/Visualizer/skills/model-visualizer/ in the package installation directory) and export <model> to <path>.html"
+```
+
+Interactive chat does not need the CLI.
+
+---
+
+## Output files
+
+```text
+<model>.html                         # standalone viewer (default)
+<model>.json                         # Model Explorer payload, when -o ends in .json
+<model>_operators.json               # flat operator export, when --operators-json is set
+<model>_subgraph_<i>.html            # one file per GPU group, when tp/pp/ep splits the model
+```
+
+A live viewer (`--serve`, default port 8765) prints `Open viewer: http://127.0.0.1:8765/` and holds the process. Ask for that only when you want a server instead of a file.
+
+---
+
+## Workflow
+
+```text
+0. Resolve the model source, output path, regime, attention, config overrides, and sharding source plus counts
+1. Install the Visualizer extra if the exporter does not import
+2. Run visualize_model_in_explorer once
+3. Confirm the HTML contains model-explorer-visualizer, or the JSON has graphCollections
+4. Report the absolute path (or the viewer URL)
+```
+
+The procedure and footguns are in [reference.md](skills/model-visualizer/reference.md).
+
+| Choice | What the skill does |
+| --- | --- |
+| Save a file | `visualize_model_in_explorer <model> -o <file>.html` |
+| JSON, then HTML | `-o model.json`, then `--from-payload model.json -o model.html` |
+| Hugging Face sharding | `--tp`, `--pp`, `--ep` and no `--engine` |
+| vLLM or SGLang sharding | `--engine vllm` or `--engine sglang` with `--tp`, `--pp`, `--ep` |
+| Attention implementation | `--attention` (`eager`, `sdpa`, `flash_attention_2`, …). Omit it to keep the checkpoint's setting |
+| Config overrides | repeat `--config-override KEY=VALUE` |
+| Decode or packed tokens | `--phase decode`, `--sequence-layout packed` |
+| Skip shapes or the meta pass | `--no-shapes`, `--no-meta-shapes` |
+
+`--device` selects which accelerator branches the drawing follows (`hip` by default). It does not select the machine that runs the export.
+
+---
+
+## Tests
+
+Skill routing and behavior cases live in [skills/model-visualizer/evals/](skills/model-visualizer/evals/README.md). Structural checks run in CI through `.github/workflows/skill-evals.yml`. The exporter's own unit tests stay in `tests/Visualizer/` and `tests/ModelUtils/`:
+
+```bash
+pip install -e ".[Visualizer,dev]"
+python3 -m pytest tests/Visualizer/ tests/ModelUtils/
+```

+# Model roofline projection
+
+Drive **`TraceLens_model_roofline_projection`** so a Hugging Face checkpoint, a local checkpoint directory, or a whitelisted modeling repo gets a kernel-by-kernel roofline table and a model-level rollup, without a trace and without a GPU run. The tool builds the same merged Model Explorer graph the visualizer draws (statically parsing `modeling_*.py`), stops expansion at every op with a direct `TraceLens.PerfModel` formula, and costs each one's FLOPs/bytes against an optional GPU architecture spec.
+
+## Full procedure
+
+Follow **[reference.md](reference.md)** for every step: inputs, install check, the single CLI invocation, GPU architecture selection, device sharding, output formats, verification, and footguns. The flag list and op-coverage caveats live in [the how-to guide](../../../../../docs/how-to/generate-model-roofline-projection.md).
+
+## Workflow index
+
+```
+0. Resolve every stated option (source, shape, GPU arch, sharding source and counts, output format)
+1. Ensure the Visualizer extra is installed
+2. Run one TraceLens_model_roofline_projection command
+3. Confirm the table printed (or the CSV/JSON artifact) and read the rollup line
+4. Report the roofline numbers and the modeled-element coverage to the user
+```
+
+## Rules
+
+- **One tool.** Run `TraceLens_model_roofline_projection`. Fall back to `python -m TraceLens.Visualizer.model_explorer_export.roofline_cli` only when that console script is absent. Do not hand-compute FLOPs/bytes or rebuild the graph in ad-hoc Python.
+- **CPU only, no trace.** No trace file is read, no checkpoint weights are loaded, and no GPU is required. A trace that already exists is the perf-report / analysis-orchestrator workflow, not this one.
+- **Every stated option is a flag.** Walk the decision procedures in reference.md before building the command: GPU architecture, shape/dimension overrides, device sharding, config overrides, attention, and runtime regime are all first-class. An option the user named is never dropped because some other default exists.
+- **No GPU arch means no roofline time; report that, don't silently omit it.** See reference.md's [GPU architecture](reference.md#gpu-architecture) table.
+- **Unmodeled is reported, not hidden.** Surface the rollup's modeled-output-element share in the summary, not just the top-N table — see reference.md's [Step 3](reference.md#step-3-verify-and-report).
+- **Graph export and benchmarking are other skills.** A request to open the architecture in Model Explorer is `model-visualizer`. A request to collect a PyTorch profiler trace or run a benchmark is Magpie profiling. A request to analyze a trace that already exists is the analysis orchestrator.
+
+## Primary outputs
+
+- **Deliverable:** the stdout table (ranked by `total_roofline_time_us`, top 20 rows by default) plus the rollup line(s): total FLOPs/bytes, modeled vs. unmodeled op counts, modeled-output-element share, and, when a GPU arch was given, the compute-bound/memory-bound time split.
+- **Optional:** the full per-op table as CSV (`--output-csv`) or JSON with the rollup included (`--output-json`).
+
+## Skill layout
+
+`TraceLens/Agent/Visualizer/skills/model-roofline-projection/` (`SKILL.md`, `reference.md`, `skill-card.md`). Cursor project discovery reads `.cursor/skills/`; symlink or copy this folder there for automatic pickup. Headless runs should open this directory inside the installed TraceLens package.

+# Model roofline projection — reference
+
+Detailed procedure for the **model-roofline-projection** skill ([SKILL.md](SKILL.md)). Read it when executing the workflow. The full flag list and op-coverage/approximation notes are in [the how-to guide](../../../../../docs/how-to/generate-model-roofline-projection.md); this file is the decision procedure.
+
+## Contents
+
+- [Workflow](#workflow)
+- [Step 0: Resolve inputs](#step-0-resolve-inputs)
+- [Step 1: Install](#step-1-install)
+- [Step 2: Command](#step-2-command)
+- [Step 3: Verify and report](#step-3-verify-and-report)
+- [GPU architecture](#gpu-architecture)
+- [Shape and dimension overrides](#shape-and-dimension-overrides)
+- [Device sharding](#device-sharding)
+- [Config overrides, attention, and runtime regime](#config-overrides-attention-and-runtime-regime)
+- [Output formats](#output-formats)
+- [Footguns](#footguns)
+
+## Workflow
+
+```
+0. Resolve every stated option (ask only for what the prompt left out)
+1. Ensure the Visualizer extra imports
+2. Run one TraceLens_model_roofline_projection command
+3. Read the table and the rollup line(s)
+4. Report the roofline numbers and the modeled-element coverage to the user
+```
+
+The tool reuses the same `TraceLens.ModelUtils` AST backend as the model visualizer to build one merged graph (parsing `modeling_*.py`, no checkpoint weights, no GPU), then costs every op with a direct `TraceLens.PerfModel` formula against the requested shape and, when given, a GPU architecture spec. Everything else is reported as unmodeled.
+
+## Step 0: Resolve inputs
+
+Take every value the user already gave. Ask only for the gaps.
+
+| Input | Required | Default when omitted |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Model source | yes | Hugging Face id, local checkpoint directory, or `--github` plus a whitelisted repo |
+| Batch size / sequence length | no | `--batch-size 1 --seq-len 2048` |
+| A specific dimension (e.g. a decode cache length) | no | `--dim KEY=VALUE`, repeatable; wins over `--batch-size`/`--seq-len` for the same key |
+| GPU architecture | no | none — FLOPs/bytes only, no roofline time. Ask if the user wants a time projection and did not name a GPU |
+| Sharding source | no | Hugging Face plans on the checkpoint. `--engine` only when the user names vLLM or SGLang |
+| Partition counts | no | `--tp 1 --pp 1 --ep 1` (that axis stays unsplit) |
+| Runtime regime (phase, cache, sequence layout, attention, mode, device) | no | prefill, cold, rectangular, checkpoint's own attention, inference, hip |
+| Output format | no | stdout table, top 20 rows ranked by roofline time |
+
+A local directory is a checkpoint when it contains `config.json`. A path to `modeling_*.py` is `--code-path`, not the positional source. A GitHub repo that is not already whitelisted needs `--allow-repo OWNER/REPO` or `TRACELENS_ALLOWED_GITHUB_REPOS`. Gated Hugging Face repos need `HF_TOKEN` in the environment. Do not invent a token.
+
+Before writing the command, walk [GPU architecture](#gpu-architecture), [Device sharding](#device-sharding), and [Config overrides, attention, and runtime regime](#config-overrides-attention-and-runtime-regime). Each option the user named becomes a flag. An option they left out stays at the tool's default.
+
+## Step 1: Install
+
+Check the exporter before doing anything else:
+
+```bash
+python -c "import TraceLens.Visualizer.model_explorer_export.roofline_cli"
+```
+
+When that import fails, install the extra from a source checkout:
+
+```bash
+pip install -e ".[Visualizer]"
+```
+
+When the checkout is not the current directory, install the package extra instead:
+
+```bash
+pip install "TraceLens[Visualizer]"
+```
+
+Python 3.10 or newer. The extra pulls `torch`, `transformers`, and `huggingface_hub`. Do not `pip install` those yourself, and do not install a ROCm or CUDA wheel: the meta-device shape pass allocates no real tensors and the roofline projection itself makes no device calls at all.
+
+Confirm the console script:
+
+```bash
+TraceLens_model_roofline_projection --help
+```
+
+If the script is missing but the import works, call `python -m TraceLens.Visualizer.model_explorer_export.roofline_cli` with the same arguments.
+
+## Step 2: Command
+
+Run one command.
+
+FLOPs/bytes only, no GPU time (the user did not name hardware):
+
+```bash
+TraceLens_model_roofline_projection <model> --batch-size 1 --seq-len 4096
+```
+
+With a bounded roofline time against a named GPU:
+
+```bash
+TraceLens_model_roofline_projection <model> \
+    --batch-size 1 --seq-len 4096 \
+    --gpu-arch-name MI300X
+```
+
+One GPU's share under a sharded deployment, same split the visualizer draws:
+
+```bash
+TraceLens_model_roofline_projection MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
+    --engine vllm --tp 2 --ep 4 \
+    --batch-size 1 --seq-len 2048 \
+    --gpu-arch-name MI325X
+```
+
+A decode step at a specific cache length, with a custom GPU arch file:
+
+```bash
+TraceLens_model_roofline_projection <model> \
+    --phase decode --dim past_len=1024 \
+    --gpu-arch-json-path ./mi300x.json
+```
+
+`<model>` is a Hugging Face id or a local checkpoint directory. `1` on any of `--tp`/`--pp`/`--ep` leaves that axis unsplit (a single, unsharded GPU). A partition count that does not divide the model evenly is still exported, with a warning on stdout — report it rather than silently rerunning with a different count.
+
+## Step 3: Verify and report
+
+Success is exit code 0 and a printed table. Read, in order:
+
+1. The table itself (ranked by `total_roofline_time_us`, top 20 rows unless `--top-n` changed that), for the hottest ops.
+2. The `Total:` line: total FLOPs, total bytes, modeled vs. unmodeled op counts, and the modeled-output-element share. Report this share — it is how much of the model the projection actually accounts for, not a detail to drop.
+3. The `Roofline time:` line, when a GPU arch was given: total roofline time plus the compute-bound/memory-bound split. Its absence (`No --gpu-arch-name/--gpu-arch-json-path given...`) means report FLOPs/bytes only and say why there is no time estimate.
+
+On a non-zero exit, show stderr to the user (`Error loading architecture: ...`). Retry once only when the error is a missing modeling file and a documented source switch fixes it (`--code-path`, `--github` with `--allow-repo`, or `--engine`).
+
+## GPU architecture
+
+| User named | Pass |
+| --- | --- |
+| A bundled GPU (`MI300X`, `MI325X`) | `--gpu-arch-name MI300X` |
+| A custom or measured arch spec | `--gpu-arch-json-path PATH` (same JSON schema; takes precedence over `--gpu-arch-name`) |
+| Nothing about hardware | omit both. FLOPs/bytes are still printed; the rollup says no roofline time was computed |
+
+Do not guess a GPU the user did not name. Ask, unless the request is explicitly "just the FLOPs" or "just the bytes".
+
+## Shape and dimension overrides
+
+`--batch-size` and `--seq-len` set the common two axes. `--dim KEY=VALUE` (repeatable) overrides one named symbolic dimension directly and wins over `--batch-size`/`--seq-len` for that same key — use it for anything the two flags do not name (a cache length, an expert count override that is not already a sharding axis, etc.).
+
+```bash
+--dim past_len=1024
+```
+
+A `--dim` value must parse as an int; the tool raises a usage error otherwise.
+
+## Device sharding
+
+Identical semantics to the model visualizer: `--tp`, `--pp`, and `--ep` are the partition counts, `--engine` chooses whose plan those counts are applied to, and a count of 1 leaves that axis unsplit.
+
+| User named | What to pass |
+| --- | --- |
+| Nothing about an engine, or "Hugging Face", "transformers", or "the checkpoint's plan" | no `--engine`. The split is `base_model_tp_plan`, `base_model_pp_plan`, and `base_model_ep_plan`, plus the causal-LM head |
+| vLLM | `--engine vllm` plus the counts |
+| SGLang | `--engine sglang` plus the counts |
+
+Each GEMM is costed at its per-GPU local shape (a column-sharded projection's output divided by the TP count, an expert stack's expert count divided by the EP count, ...), derived from the same shape-inference engine the visualizer uses against a locally-divided config — not a second, independently-matched approximation.
+
+## Config overrides, attention, and runtime regime
+
+Same flags and precedence rules as the model visualizer: `--config-override KEY=VALUE` (repeatable, dotted keys reach nested configs, last value wins), `--attention` (leave unset to keep the checkpoint's own implementation), `--phase`/`--cache`/`--sequence-layout`/`--mode`/`--device` for the runtime regime. An option the user named is never dropped because some other default exists. See the model-visualizer skill's [reference.md](../model-visualizer/reference.md#config-overrides) for the full decision tables; they apply unchanged here.
+
+## Output formats
+
+| User asked for | Flag |
+| --- | --- |
+| Just the printed table | nothing extra; adjust `--top-n` (default 20, `0` for every row) |
+| The full per-op table as a file | `--output-csv PATH` |
+| The full per-op table plus the rollup as JSON | `--output-json PATH` |
+| A display name for the architecture | `--title "..."` |
+
+`--output-csv`/`--output-json` do not suppress the stdout table; both are written in addition to it.
+
+## Footguns
+
+- **No GPU arch means no time, not an error.** A run with neither `--gpu-arch-name` nor `--gpu-arch-json-path` exits 0 and prints FLOPs/bytes with an explicit "no roofline time" line. That is expected, not a bug to retry.
+- **Unmodeled is not a failure mode.** Embeddings, convolutions, reshapes, and anything else with no direct `TraceLens.PerfModel` formula are reported, not silently skipped. A low "% of output elements modeled" is a real statement about coverage for that architecture, not a tool error — surface it rather than chasing 100%.
+- **MoE routing is approximated as `experts_per_tok` GEMM passes**, never `num_experts`; the router's own softmax/top-k and any shared-expert add are not separately costed. State this when a MoE model's rollup is the headline number.
+- **`--device` is not the host.** As with the visualizer, the default `hip` means the drawing follows HIP branches in the modeling source. The projection still runs on CPU regardless of this flag.
+- **`--engine` and a named source do different jobs.** `--code-path` or `--github` picks the modeling file; `--engine` still picks the plan parser for the partition counts. Omit `--engine` for a Hugging Face plan; pass it for vLLM or SGLang even when the file is local.
+- **This is not a trace tool.** No `.json`/`.pftrace` profiler trace is read here. A request to analyze a trace that already exists is the analysis orchestrator, not this skill.
+- **GEMM bias, norm affine-ness, and SDPA causality are assumed**, not read from the checkpoint in every case (GEMM bias assumed absent; every norm assumed affine, RMSNorm bias-free; SDPA assumed causal exactly when query and key/value sequence lengths resolve equal). See the how-to guide's "Known approximations" for the full list before treating a number as exact.

+# Model visualizer
+
+Drive **`visualize_model_in_explorer`** so a Hugging Face checkpoint, a local checkpoint directory, or a whitelisted modeling repo becomes one Model Explorer graph. The export is static analysis plus an optional meta-device shape pass. It runs on CPU and does not load checkpoint weights.
+
+## Full procedure
+
+Follow **[reference.md](reference.md)** for every step: inputs, install check, the single CLI invocation, config overrides, attention selection, Hugging Face / vLLM / SGLang sharding, the other flags, verification, and footguns. The tool's long flag list lives in [the Visualizer README](../../../../Visualizer/README.md).
+
+## Workflow index
+
+```
+0. Resolve every stated option (source, output, viewer, regime, attention, config overrides, sharding source and counts)
+1. Ensure the Visualizer extra is installed
+2. Run one visualize_model_in_explorer command
+3. Confirm the HTML or JSON artifact (or the viewer URL)
+4. Tell the user the path or URL
+```
+
+## Rules
+
+- **One exporter.** Run `visualize_model_in_explorer`. Fall back to `python -m TraceLens.Visualizer.model_explorer_export.cli` only when that console script is absent. Do not rebuild the graph in ad-hoc Python.
+- **CPU only.** Do not request a GPU, set `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, or download weight shards. Config and modeling source are enough.
+- **Every stated option is a flag.** Walk the decision procedures in reference.md before building the command. Config overrides, the attention implementation, and Hugging Face versus vLLM versus SGLang sharding are first-class. An option the user named is never dropped because some other default exists.
+- **Default artifact.** Write a self-contained `.html` file. Add `--serve` only when the user asks to view the graph live.
+- **Defaults stay on** unless the user opts out: `--auto-venv`, `--meta-shapes`, symbolic shapes, `--drop-constants` for HTML. Leave `--attention` unset when the user did not name an implementation, so the checkpoint's own setting survives.
+- **`--device` is the accelerator being drawn** (default `hip`). It does not probe the machine running the export.
+- **Traces and benchmarks** are other skills. A `.json` Chrome trace, a request for `analysis.md`, or a Magpie profiling run is not this workflow.
+
+## Primary outputs
+
+- **Deliverable:** `<model>.html` in the working directory, or the path passed with `-o`. Device partitions write `*_subgraph_<i>.html` beside it.
+- **Optional:** payload `.json` (`-o model.json`), operator JSON (`--operators-json`), or a local viewer URL when `--serve` was requested.
+
+## Skill layout
+
+`TraceLens/Agent/Visualizer/skills/model-visualizer/` (`SKILL.md`, `reference.md`, `skill-card.md`). Cursor project discovery reads `.cursor/skills/`; symlink or copy this folder there for automatic pickup. Headless runs should open this directory inside the installed TraceLens package.

+# Model visualizer — reference
+
+Detailed procedure for the **model-visualizer** skill ([SKILL.md](SKILL.md)). Read it when executing the workflow. The exporter's full flag list is in [the Visualizer README](../../../../Visualizer/README.md); this file is the decision procedure.
+
+## Contents
+
+- [Workflow](#workflow)
+- [Step 0: Resolve inputs](#step-0-resolve-inputs)
+- [Step 1: Install](#step-1-install)
+- [Step 2: Command](#step-2-command)
+- [Step 3: Verify](#step-3-verify)
+- [Config overrides](#config-overrides)
+- [Attention implementation](#attention-implementation)
+- [Device sharding](#device-sharding)
+- [Other flags](#other-flags)
+- [Footguns](#footguns)
+
+## Workflow
+
+```
+0. Resolve every stated option (ask only for what the prompt left out)
+1. Ensure the Visualizer extra imports
+2. Run one visualize_model_in_explorer command
+3. Confirm the artifact or viewer URL
+4. Report that path or URL to the user
+```
+
+The graph is built by parsing `modeling_*.py` with the Python `ast` module (`TraceLens.ModelUtils`) and, by default, a PyTorch meta-device pass that fills shapes static analysis cannot infer. No checkpoint weights are loaded and no GPU is used.
+
+## Step 0: Resolve inputs
+
+Take every value the user already gave. Ask only for the gaps.
+
+| Input | Required | Default when omitted |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Model source | yes | Hugging Face id, local checkpoint directory, or `--github` plus a whitelisted repo |
+| Output path | no | `<model-id-with-slashes-replaced>.html` in the working directory |
+| Live viewer | no | HTML file only. `--serve` only if the user asked to open or serve the graph |
+| Regime | no | rectangular, prefill, cold cache, inference, `--device hip` |
+| Attention | no | unset, so the checkpoint's `_attn_implementation` is used (`sdpa` when that key is absent) |
+| Config overrides | no | none. Pass one `--config-override` per key the user named |
+| Sharding source | no | Hugging Face plans on the checkpoint. `--engine` only when the user names vLLM or SGLang |
+| Partition counts | no | `--tp 1 --pp 1 --ep 1` (that axis stays unsplit) |
+| Shapes | no | on (`--no-shapes` only when the user asks to skip them) |
+
+Before writing the command, walk [Config overrides](#config-overrides), [Attention implementation](#attention-implementation), [Device sharding](#device-sharding), and [Other flags](#other-flags). Each option the user named becomes a flag. An option they left out stays at the exporter default. Do not pass a default that would overrule the checkpoint: leaving `--attention` unset is what preserves a checkpoint that asks for something other than `sdpa`.
+
+A local directory is a checkpoint when it contains `config.json`. A path to `modeling_*.py` is `--code-path`, not the positional source. A GitHub repo that is not already whitelisted needs `--allow-repo OWNER/REPO` or `TRACELENS_ALLOWED_GITHUB_REPOS`.
+
+Gated Hugging Face repos need `HF_TOKEN` in the environment. Do not invent a token.
+
+## Step 1: Install
+
+Check the exporter before doing anything else:
+
+```bash
+python -c "import TraceLens.Visualizer.model_explorer_export.cli"
+```
+
+When that import fails, install the extra from a source checkout:
+
+```bash
+pip install -e ".[Visualizer]"
+```
+
+When the checkout is not the current directory, install the package extra instead:
+
+```bash
+pip install "TraceLens[Visualizer]"
+```
+
+Python 3.10 or newer. The extra pulls `torch`, `transformers`, and `huggingface_hub`. Do not `pip install` those yourself, and do not install a ROCm or CUDA wheel. The meta-device pass allocates no real tensors.
+
+Confirm the console script:
+
+```bash
+visualize_model_in_explorer --help
+```
+
+If the script is missing but the import works, call `python -m TraceLens.Visualizer.model_explorer_export.cli` with the same arguments.
+
+## Step 2: Command
+
+Run one command. Prefer the console script.
+
+HTML file (the usual request):
+
+```bash
+visualize_model_in_explorer <model> -o <path>.html
+```
+
+`<model>` is a Hugging Face id or a local checkpoint directory. Omit `-o` to write `<model-with-slashes-as-underscores>.html` in the working directory.
+
+Payload JSON, then HTML, when the user wants both artifacts. Stage 2 does not load the model:
+
+```bash
+visualize_model_in_explorer <model> -o <path>.json
+visualize_model_in_explorer --from-payload <path>.json -o <path>.html
+```
+
+Live viewer, only when the user asked to serve or open it:
+
+```bash
+visualize_model_in_explorer <model> --serve --port 8765
+```
+
+`--open` implies `--serve` and also launches a browser. The server process blocks. Print the `Open viewer:` URL to the user before treating the command as finished. Do not start a server for an HTML-only request.
+
+Operator list with inferred shapes, in addition to the graph:
+
+```bash
+visualize_model_in_explorer <model> -o <path>.html --operators-json <path>_operators.json
+```
+
+Examples, one per sharding source, plus overrides and attention together:
+
+```bash
+visualize_model_in_explorer moonshotai/Kimi-K3 -o kimi.html
+
+visualize_model_in_explorer meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B \
+  --tp 8 --pp 2 -o llama-hf.html
+
+visualize_model_in_explorer meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B \
+  --engine vllm --tp 8 --pp 2 -o llama-vllm.html
+
+visualize_model_in_explorer MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-flash \
+  --engine sglang --tp 2 --ep 4 -o minimax.html
+
+visualize_model_in_explorer moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
+  --sequence-layout packed --phase decode --attention eager \
+  --config-override num_hidden_layers=2 \
+  -o kimi-decode.html
+
+visualize_model_in_explorer /models/qwen \
+  --sequence-layout packed --phase decode -o /models/qwen/qwen-decode.html
+```
+
+The first Llama command uses the checkpoint's Hugging Face plans. The second draws vLLM's pinned modeling source. The third draws SGLang's. See [Device sharding](#device-sharding) for when `--engine` still changes the plan parser after `--code-path` or `--github` names the file. vLLM is pinned at `vllm-project/vllm@v0.32.0`. SGLang is pinned at `sgl-project/sglang@v0.5.22`.
+
+A partition count that does not divide the model evenly is still exported, with a warning on stdout. More than one GPU group writes `<stem>_subgraph_<i>.html`.
+
+## Step 3: Verify
+
+Success for a file write is exit code 0 and a line `Wrote standalone viewer:` (HTML) or `Wrote Model Explorer JSON:` (JSON).
+
+Then check the file:
+
+- HTML: non-empty, and the text contains both `model-explorer-visualizer` and `graphCollections`.
+- JSON: non-empty, and it parses as an object with a non-empty `graphCollections` array.
+- Several GPU groups: every `*_subgraph_*.html` named on stdout exists.
+
+Report the absolute path. For `--serve`, report the URL from `Open viewer:`.
+
+On a non-zero exit, show stderr to the user. Retry once only when the error is a missing modeling file and a documented source switch fixes it (`--code-path`, `--github` with `--allow-repo`, or `--engine`). Leave `--auto-venv` and `--meta-shapes` on. `--no-meta-shapes` is a pure-static fallback only after the user accepts shapes that static analysis could not fill.
+
+The first open of an HTML file loads `<model-explorer-visualizer>` and its font textures from unpkg. The layout worker is embedded. Tell the user that opening the file needs network once, unless the browser already cached that package.
+
+## Config overrides
+
+`--config-override` is the last word on a config value. Use it for every config key the user named, except the attention implementation, which is [`--attention`](#attention-implementation).
+
+Pass one flag per key, repeated:
+
+```bash
+--config-override num_hidden_layers=2 --config-override vision_config.hidden_size=1024
+```
+
+Rules:
+
+- The key is a field on the checkpoint config. A dotted key writes a nested block (`vision_config.hidden_size` reaches `vision_config["hidden_size"]`). When the parent is not a dict, the dotted string is stored as a single key.
+- The value is JSON when it parses, and plain text otherwise. `8`, `true`, `false`, `null`, and `[1, 2]` mean what they mean in `config.json`. `torch_dtype=bfloat16` needs no extra quotes. +

+| User named | Pass |
+| --- | --- |
+| Nothing about attention | omit `--attention`. The checkpoint's `_attn_implementation` is used. A silent config is `sdpa` |
+| eager, "matmul and softmax", the unfused path | `--attention eager` |

+| flash attention 2, FA2 | `--attention flash_attention_2` |
+| flash attention 3, FA3 | `--attention flash_attention_3` |
+| flash attention or flash attn, with no version | `--attention flash_attention` |
+| `flash_attn`, `flash_attn_2`, or `kernels-community/flash-attn` | that string, unchanged |

+## Device sharding
+
+`--tp`, `--pp`, and `--ep` are the partition counts. `--engine` chooses whose plan those counts are applied to. The three axes combine. A count of 1 leaves that axis unsplit, so omit a flag the user left at one GPU.

+| --- | --- |

+
+Pass a flag only when the user asked for that behavior. +| A JSON payload | `-o <file>.json` |
+| HTML from a payload already written | `--from-payload <file>.json -o <file>.html` (this skips loading the model) |
+| A live viewer | `--serve`, and `--open` only when they asked to open a browser |

+| One new token | `--phase decode` (decode always reads a cache) |

+| No symbolic shapes | `--no-shapes` |
+| Skip the meta-device pass | `--no-meta-shapes` |
+| Stay on the installed transformers | `--no-auto-venv` |
+| Weight and constant nodes in the HTML | `--no-drop-constants` (JSON always keeps them) |

+| Modeling source from GitHub | `--github`, plus `--allow-repo` when the repo is not already allowed |
+| A flat operator list | `--operators-json PATH` |
+| Opaque modules, no internal steps | `--no-inline-expansion` |

+
+## Footguns
+
+- **`--device` is not the host.** Default `hip` means the drawing follows HIP branches in the modeling source. The export still runs on CPU. Do not change it because the current machine is NVIDIA, CPU-only, or an NPU.
+- **`--auto-venv` may re-exec.** A checkpoint whose `transformers` pin differs from the installed one is exported in a cached environment. That re-exec is success, not a failure. Disable it only with `--no-auto-venv`.
+- **HTML drops constants by default.** Learned weights and buffers stay in the JSON payload and disappear from HTML. Pass `--no-drop-constants` when the user wants those nodes on the page.
+- **unpkg on first open.** The HTML file embeds the graph and the layout worker. The visualizer element itself still loads from unpkg the first time the file is opened.
+- **Do not download weights.** `huggingface_hub` fetches `config.json` and modeling source. A multi-gigabyte weight download means the wrong tool was invoked.
+- **Server calls block.** `--serve` and `--open` do not return until the process is interrupted. Prefer `-o file.html` unless a live viewer was requested.

+"""Shared argparse groups and ``ArchitectureSpec`` loading for ModelUtils CLIs.
+
+Every CLI that loads a checkpoint through the AST backend (Model Explorer
+export, the roofline projection tool, ...) needs the same checkpoint-provenance,
+basic-op-filter, and runtime-regime flags. Defining them once here keeps the
+flags and their help text from drifting between tools.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from TraceLens.ModelUtils.ast_analyze import RuntimeRegime
+from TraceLens.ModelUtils.basic_ops import DEFAULT_BASIC_OP_PATTERNS, BasicOpFilter
+from TraceLens.ModelUtils.extract import ArchitectureSpec, parse_config_overrides
+from TraceLens.ModelUtils.loader import (
+    build_detailed_basic_ops,
+    build_roofline_basic_ops,
+    load_model_spec,
+)
+
+
+def add_model_source_arguments(
+    parser: argparse.ArgumentParser,
+) -> argparse._ArgumentGroup:
+    """Add the "model source options" group: checkpoint provenance and basic-op filters."""
+    group = parser.add_argument_group("model source options")
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--github",
+        "-g",
+        help=(
+            "Optional GitHub repo URL or github:owner/repo@ref:path for modeling source "
+            "when the HF repo does not ship modeling_*.py (repo must be whitelisted)"
+        ),
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--allow-repo",
+        action="append",
+        default=[],
+        metavar="OWNER/REPO",
+        help=(
+            "Whitelist an extra GitHub repository for remote source introspection "
+            "(repeatable; huggingface/transformers is allowed by default)"
+        ),
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--config-path",
+        help="Explicit config.json path inside the checkpoint",
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--code-path",
+        type=Path,
+        help="Explicit path to modeling_*.py when auto-discovery is insufficient",
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--basic-op-add",
+        action="append",
+        default=[],
+        metavar="REGEX",
+        help=(
+            "Regex for block names treated as basic leaf operations "
+            f"(repeatable; defaults: {', '.join(DEFAULT_BASIC_OP_PATTERNS)})"
+        ),
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--basic-op-remove",
+        action="append",
+        default=[],
+        metavar="REGEX",
+        help="Remove a default basic-op regex (repeatable; pass exact pattern text)",
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--meta-shapes",
+        dest="meta_shapes",
+        action="store_true",
+        default=True,
+        help=(
+            "Run a meta-device forward pass (requires torch + transformers) to "
+            "capture ground-truth shapes for nn.Module layers AND for inline "
+            "operations the static analysis can't resolve (default: on)"
+        ),
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--no-meta-shapes",
+        dest="meta_shapes",
+        action="store_false",
+        help="Disable torch-assisted shape inference (pure static analysis)",
+    )
+    return group
+
+
+def add_roofline_op_boundary_argument(
+    parser: argparse.ArgumentParser,
+    *,
+    group: argparse._ArgumentGroup | None = None,
+    default: bool = True,
+) -> argparse._ArgumentGroup:
+    """Add ``--stop-at-roofline-ops`` to *group* (a new "model source options" group by default).
+
+    Tools that always want this behavior (the roofline projection CLI) should
+    not add this flag at all and instead pass ``stop_at_roofline_ops=True``
+    directly to :func:`load_architecture_spec_from_args`.
+    """
+    group = group or parser.add_argument_group("model source options")
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--stop-at-roofline-ops",
+        dest="stop_at_roofline_ops",
+        action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction,
+        default=default,
+        help=(
+            "Stop expanding a module once it matches an op with a TraceLens.PerfModel "
+            "formula (Linear, Conv, RMSNorm/LayerNorm/GroupNorm/BatchNorm/InstanceNorm, "
+            "Softmax), instead of continuing into its internal primitive steps "
+            f"(default: {'on' if default else 'off'})."
+        ),
+    )
+    return group
+
+
+def add_runtime_regime_arguments(
+    parser: argparse.ArgumentParser,
+) -> argparse._ArgumentGroup:
+    """Add the "runtime regime" group: which forward-pass arm the export depicts."""
+    group = parser.add_argument_group(
+        "runtime regime",
+        "Which RUN the export depicts. A forward branches on things no config "
+        "decides and only a run does, and both arms are real: drawing both "
+        "leaves every shape below the branch true of only one of them. Each "
+        "option picks exactly one arm, so the arm not taken is never used.",
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--sequence-layout",
+        choices=list(RuntimeRegime.SEQUENCE_LAYOUTS),
+        default=RuntimeRegime.SEQUENCE_LAYOUTS[0],
+        help=(
+            "rectangular keeps [B, S, ...]; packed removes the padding first "
+            "and carries every real token as one row, [1, nnz, ...] "
+            "(default: rectangular)."
+        ),
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--phase",
+        choices=list(RuntimeRegime.PHASES),
+        default=RuntimeRegime.PHASES[0],
+        help=(
+            "prefill scores a whole prompt; decode advances one token, which "
+            "is what makes the query length 1 and can select different kernels "
+            "entirely (default: prefill)."
+        ),
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--cache",
+        choices=list(RuntimeRegime.CACHES),
+        default=RuntimeRegime.CACHES[0],
+        help=(
+            "cold is the first forward, with nothing stored yet; warm "
+            "continues from a cache that already holds keys and values "
+            "(default: cold). decode always reads a cache."
+        ),
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--attention",
+        default=None,
+        help=(
+            "Attention implementation to draw (eager, sdpa, "
+            "flash_attention_2, ...). eager draws the real matmul/softmax "
+            "chain where sdpa draws one fused kernel. Unset takes the "
+            "checkpoint's own setting, which is sdpa unless it says otherwise."
+        ),
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--mode",
+        choices=list(RuntimeRegime.MODES),
+        default=RuntimeRegime.MODES[0],
+        help="Whether `self.training` reads true (default: inference).",
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--device",
+        choices=list(RuntimeRegime.DEVICES),
+        default=RuntimeRegime.DEVICES[0],
+        help=(
+            "The accelerator being modeled, for files that branch on "
+            "is_npu()/is_cuda()/is_hip()/... at import time. Stated, never "
+            "detected: this never probes the machine running the export "
+            "(default: hip, this repo's own vendor)."
+        ),
+    )
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--config-override",
+        action="append",
+        metavar="KEY=VALUE",
+        default=[],
+        help=(
+            "Override one config key, repeatable. Applied left to right over "
+            "everything else -- the checkpoint, the config class defaults and "
+            "the model's own constructor writes -- so this is the last word. "
+            "A dotted key reaches a nested config "
+            "(vision_config.hidden_size=1024); the value is read as JSON when "
+            "it parses as one (8, true, null, [1, 2]) and as text otherwise. "
+            "Stating one key twice warns and keeps the last."
+        ),
+    )
+    return group
+
+
+def add_engine_argument(
+    parser: argparse.ArgumentParser,
+    *,
+    group: argparse._ArgumentGroup | None = None,
+) -> argparse._ArgumentGroup:
+    """Add just ``--engine`` to *group* (a new "model source options" group by default).
+
+    Pass an existing group (e.g. a caller's own "device partitions" group) to
+    keep ``--engine`` next to related flags like ``--tp``/``--pp``/``--ep``
+    instead of opening a second "model source options" section in ``--help``.
+    """
+    group = group or parser.add_argument_group("model source options")
+    group.add_argument(
+        "--engine",
+        choices=("vllm", "sglang"),
+        help=(
+            "Draw this checkpoint's architecture from vLLM's or SGLang's own "
+            "pinned modeling source (ColumnParallelLinear, make_layers, FusedMoE, "
+            "...) instead of transformers'. Ignored once --code-path / --github "
+            "already name the source."
+        ),
+    )
+    return group
+
+
+def build_runtime_regime(args: argparse.Namespace) -> RuntimeRegime:
+    """Build a :class:`RuntimeRegime` from the shared runtime-regime flags."""
+    return RuntimeRegime(
+        sequence_layout=args.sequence_layout,
+        phase=args.phase,
+        cache=args.cache,
+        attention=args.attention,
+        mode=args.mode,
+        device=args.device,
+    )
+
+
+def build_basic_ops_from_args(
+    args: argparse.Namespace,
+    *,
+    stop_at_roofline_ops: bool | None = None,
+) -> BasicOpFilter:
+    """Pick the leaf-op granularity and build its :class:`BasicOpFilter`.
+
+    ``stop_at_roofline_ops=True`` stops expansion at ops with a PerfModel formula
+    (:func:`build_roofline_basic_ops`); ``False`` uses the usual detailed-export
+    leaf set (:func:`build_detailed_basic_ops`). Defaults to
+    ``args.stop_at_roofline_ops`` when the caller added
+    :func:`add_roofline_op_boundary_argument`, else ``True``.
+    """
+    resolved = (
+        stop_at_roofline_ops
+        if stop_at_roofline_ops is not None
+        else getattr(args, "stop_at_roofline_ops", True)
+    )
+    builder = build_roofline_basic_ops if resolved else build_detailed_basic_ops
+    return builder(add=args.basic_op_add, remove=args.basic_op_remove)
+
+
+def load_architecture_spec_from_args(
+    checkpoint: str | Path | None,
+    args: argparse.Namespace,
+    *,
+    title: str | None = None,
+    stop_at_roofline_ops: bool | None = None,
+) -> ArchitectureSpec:
+    """Load an :class:`ArchitectureSpec` using the shared model-source / regime flags.
+
+    Common path for every CLI built on :func:`add_model_source_arguments` and
+    :func:`add_runtime_regime_arguments` (and, optionally, :func:`add_engine_argument`).
+    See :func:`build_basic_ops_from_args` for ``stop_at_roofline_ops``.
+    """
+    basic_ops = build_basic_ops_from_args(
+        args, stop_at_roofline_ops=stop_at_roofline_ops
+    )
+    return load_model_spec(
+        checkpoint,
+        github=args.github,
+        config_path=args.config_path,
+        code_path=args.code_path,
+        name=title,
+        analyze_code=True,
+        detailed=True,
+        basic_ops=basic_ops,
+        require_code=True,
+        allow_github_repos=args.allow_repo,
+        regime=build_runtime_regime(args),
+        config_overrides=parse_config_overrides(args.config_override),
+        engine=getattr(args, "engine", None),
+    )

+

+        q_eps         — float scalar

+        k_eps         — float scalar

+    Expected Input Dims from trace:

+        e.g. [(12, 2048), (2048,), (), (12, 512), (512,), (), (12, 2048), (12, 512)]

+        num_channels = event["args"]["Input Dims"][1][0]  # q_weight.shape[0]

+def copy_mla_v4_stage2_shapes(trace_tree):
+    for uid in list(trace_tree.name2event_uids.get(_STAGE2_KERNEL, [])):
+        kernel = trace_tree.get_UID2event(uid)
+        if kernel.get("cat") != "kernel":
+            continue
+        launcher = trace_tree.get_parent_event(kernel)
+        if launcher is None:
+            continue
+        donor = _find_donor(trace_tree, launcher)
+        if donor is None:
+            continue
+        src = donor.get("args") or {}
+        dst = launcher.setdefault("args", {})
+        for key in _ARG_KEYS:
+            if src.get(key) and not dst.get(key):
+                dst[key] = src[key]
+
+
+def _find_donor(trace_tree, start):
+    current = start
+    seen = set()
+    while current is not None and current.get("UID") not in seen:
+        seen.add(current.get("UID"))
+        if _PARENT_PY in current.get("name", ""):
+            return _find_named_descendant(trace_tree, current, _DONOR_OP)
+        current = trace_tree.get_parent_event(current)
+    return None
+
+
+def _find_named_descendant(trace_tree, event, name):
+    found = []
+
+    def walk(node):
+        for child_uid in node.get("children") or []:
+            child = trace_tree.get_UID2event(child_uid)
+            if child is None:
+                continue
+            if child.get("name") == name and child.get("cat") == "cpu_op":
+                found.append(child)
+            walk(child)
+
+    walk(event)
+    if len(found) == 1:
+        return found[0]
+    return None

+def compute_roofline_time_and_bound(gflops, bytes_moved, peak_tflops, mem_bw_gbps):
+    """Roofline-bounded time (µs) and bound type from FLOPs, bytes, and arch peaks.
+
+    The lower bound an op could achieve: whichever of compute time (flops /

+    ``(None, None)`` when any input is missing or there is no work to bound.
+
+    Args:
+        gflops: GFLOPs performed by the op.
+        bytes_moved: Bytes read + written by the op.
+        peak_tflops: Max achievable TFLOPS for the op's compute spec.
+        mem_bw_gbps: Peak HBM bandwidth in GB/s.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``(roofline_time_us, roofline_bound)`` where ``roofline_bound`` is
+        ``"COMPUTE_BOUND"`` or ``"MEMORY_BOUND"``.
+    """
+    if (
+        peak_tflops is None
+        or mem_bw_gbps is None
+        or bytes_moved is None
+        or not gflops
+        or gflops <= 0
+    ):
+        return None, None
+    # Compute time: flops / (peak_tflops * 1e12) gives seconds, convert to µs
+    compute_time_us = (gflops * 1e9 / (peak_tflops * 1e12)) * 1e6
+    # Memory time: bytes / (bandwidth_gbps * 1e9) gives seconds, convert to µs
+    memory_time_us = (bytes_moved / (mem_bw_gbps * 1e9)) * 1e6
+    roofline_bound = (
+        "COMPUTE_BOUND" if compute_time_us >= memory_time_us else "MEMORY_BOUND"
+    )
+    return max(compute_time_us, memory_time_us), roofline_bound

+    """``layer.0`` → class for a Sequential the representative element contains.
+
+    The representative is the first element. Its ``layer`` Sequential lists the
+    bottleneck convs the AST draws as one opaque tile.
+    """
+    if not descriptors:
+        return None
+    paths = dict(descriptors[0])
+    overrides: dict[str, str] = {}
+    for path, class_name in paths.items():
+        parent, _, leaf = path.rpartition(".")
+        if (
+            parent
+            and leaf.isdigit()

+def _attrs_only_on_first_element(
+    descriptors: tuple[tuple[tuple[str, str], ...], ...],
+) -> frozenset[str]:
+    """Top-level attrs whose class differs between the first element and the next.
+
+    ResNet's projection shortcut exists on the first block of a stage. The
+    graph draws that representative once, so those nodes repeat once per stage,
+    not once per block.
+    """
+    if len(descriptors) < 2:
+        return frozenset()

+    def tops(desc: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]) -> dict[str, str]:
+        return {path: class_name for path, class_name in desc if "." not in path}

+    first, second = tops(descriptors[0]), tops(descriptors[1])

+def _ensure_nested_element_trees(
+    spec: ArchitectureSpec, basic_ops: BasicOpFilter
+) -> None:
+    """Register a detail tree for each leaf element class of the nested groups.
+
+    Mirrors :func:`extract._append_vision_section_tree`: a non-uniform model's
+    stage-element classes (``ConvNextLayer``) are fully parsed in the registry but
+    are not among the top-level export sections, so build each once and append it
+    so :func:`_append_section` can expand it by class.
+    """
+
+    def walk(group: RepeatedGroup):
+        yield group
+        for child in group.children:
+            yield from walk(child)
+
+    existing = {tree.class_name for _label, tree in spec.export_block_trees}
+    for root in spec.nested_module_groups:
+        for group in walk(root):
+            # Only classes we actually expand. A parent stage is a container,
+            # not a tile; its leaf body and each pipeline member are.
+            if group.children:
+                class_names: list[str] = []
+            elif group.element_classes:
+                class_names = list(group.element_classes)
+            elif group.element_class:
+                class_names = [group.element_class]
+            else:
+                class_names = []
+            overrides = _container_class_overrides(group.descriptors)
+            for class_name in class_names:
+                if class_name in existing:
+                    continue
+                tree = build_block_node(
+                    attr_name=class_name,
+                    class_name=class_name,
+                    registry=spec.class_registry,
+                    basic_ops=basic_ops,
+                    infer_init_steps=True,
+                    class_overrides=overrides,
+                )
+                spec.export_block_trees.append((class_name, tree))
+                existing.add(class_name)
+            # A stage module that is not itself a repeated group (Swin patch
+            # merging) still needs a detail tree so the side tile expands.
+            child_attrs = {
+                repeated_child_attr(group, child) for child in group.children
+            }
+            for desc in group.descriptors:
+                for path, class_name in desc:
+                    if "." in path or path in child_attrs or class_name in existing:
+                        continue
+                    if class_name in {"Sequential", "ModuleList", "Identity"}:
+                        continue
+                    if class_name not in spec.class_registry:
+                        continue
+                    tree = build_block_node(
+                        attr_name=class_name,
+                        class_name=class_name,
+                        registry=spec.class_registry,
+                        basic_ops=basic_ops,
+                        infer_init_steps=True,
+                    )
+                    spec.export_block_trees.append((class_name, tree))
+                    existing.add(class_name)

+def _child_meta_path(parent: RepeatedGroup, pos: int, child: RepeatedGroup) -> str:
+    """Live module path of *child* at parent position *pos* (fills the collapsed ``*``)."""
+    suffix = child.path[len(parent.path) :]  # ".*.layers"
+    if suffix.startswith(".*"):
+        return f"{parent.path}.{pos}{suffix[2:]}"
+    return child.path

+def _stamp_meta_path(
+    nodes: list[dict[str, Any]], first_index: int, meta_path: str
+) -> None:
+    """Tag every node just emitted with its live module path.
+
+    The path carries the stage index. Shape attachment matches a node to the
+    captured module whose dotted suffix appears in the node id, so a boundary
+    tile and the conv next to it share one concrete ``[B, C, H, W]``.
+    """
+    if not meta_path:
+        return
+    for node in nodes[first_index:]:
+        attrs = node.setdefault("attrs", [])
+        if not isinstance(attrs, list):
+            continue
+        if any(item.get("key") == "meta_path" for item in attrs):
+            continue
+        attrs.append({"key": "meta_path", "value": meta_path})
+
+
+def _stamp_repeat_count(
+    nodes: list[dict[str, Any]],
+    first_index: int,
+    count: int,
+    once_attrs: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
+) -> None:
+    """Record how many live modules this drawn node stands for.
+
+    The stage namespace is ``s2_27x_...`` so a parser that only accepts a
+    segment starting with ``{N}x_`` would count the stage once. The attr is the
+    count those parsers read. An attr that exists only on the first element
+    (the projection shortcut) is drawn on the representative and counted once.
+    """
+    for node in nodes[first_index:]:
+        ident = f"{node.get('id', '')} {node.get('namespace', '')}".lower()
+        value = "1" if any(attr.lower() in ident for attr in once_attrs) else str(count)
+        attrs = node.setdefault("attrs", [])
+        if not isinstance(attrs, list):
+            continue
+        current = next(
+            (item for item in attrs if item.get("key") == "repeat_count"), None
+        )
+        if current is None:
+            attrs.append({"key": "repeat_count", "value": value})
+        else:
+            current["value"] = value
+

+def _stage_banner(stage_index: tuple[int, ...], text: str) -> str:
+    """Prefix a repeated-body or leading-node label with its stage index."""
+    if not stage_index:

+def _append_pipeline_members(

+    group: RepeatedGroup,

+def _stage_position_steps(
+    spec: ArchitectureSpec, group: RepeatedGroup, pos: int

+    next stage to the pre-downsample tensor.
+    """

+    child_attrs = {repeated_child_attr(group, child) for child in children}
+    owner = (getattr(spec, "class_registry", None) or {}).get(group.element_class)
+    calls = list(getattr(owner, "forward_calls", None) or [])
+    steps: list[tuple[int, int, str, Any]] = []
+    for index, child in enumerate(children):
