+"""Augment the analysis-orchestrator's compute findings with an analytical,
+config-derived roofline for kernels the trace could not model.
+
+The trace-based perf report models an op only when the trace carries its Input
+Dims (``record_shapes=True``) *and* PerfModel has a formula for it. A model's
+bespoke kernels -- a custom attention or fused-MoE -- therefore fall through as
+"heuristic / unmodeled", and the orchestrator can only rank them by E2E
+GPU-time share, with no bound classification or roofline floor.
+
+This utility closes that gap *without* needing trace shapes. It runs TraceLens's
+model-explorer roofline (:func:`...roofline_cli.run_projection`), which derives
+op shapes from the model config, at one or more runtime regimes (decode/prefill,
+batch, context). It maps the dominant unmodeled kernel of each roofline category
+(Attention, MoE, ...) to the matching orchestrator finding by kernel name, then:
+
+- writes ``metadata/roofline_augmentation.json`` (the full record), and
+- merges an additive ``roofline`` block onto the matching
+  ``priority_data.json::findings[]`` entry (:func:`merge_into_priority_data`),
+  leaving every existing field untouched.
+
+The orchestrator does not invent the regime. A sub-agent writes
+``metadata/roofline_augment_args.json`` from the trace artifacts, and this
+script projects each phase in that file. A direct CLI remains for a single
+regime. Must run after Step 8.5 (``generate_priority_data``), which regenerates
+``priority_data.json``.
+
+CLI::
+
+    python -m TraceLens.Visualizer.model_explorer_export.roofline_augment \\
+      --output-dir <orchestrator_output_dir> \\
+      --args-json <orchestrator_output_dir>/metadata/roofline_augment_args.json
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import glob
+import json
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+# Substrings (lowercased) in a KERNEL NAME that identify its roofline op
+# category. Name-based, not module-based: a bare projection GEMM launched from
+# an attention module is a GEMM, not the attention core, so matching on the
+# module chain would mis-map it. A GEMM kernel maps to "GEMM" (and is dropped
+# when the roofline has no standalone GEMM category, i.e. projections are folded
+# into the attention/MoE boundary ops).
+_CATEGORY_MATCHERS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
+    "Attention": ("rel_attention", "flash_attn", "fmha", "sdpa", "_attn_", "attention"),
+    "MoE": ("fused_moe", "moe_", "_moe", "grouped_gemm", "expert"),
+    "GEMM": ("cijk", "tensile", "cutlass", "::mm", "addmm", "gemm"),
+}
+
+
+def classify_kernel(kernel_name: str | None, module_chain: Any = None) -> str | None:
+    """Map a trace kernel to a roofline op category by its NAME.
+
+    Attention/MoE win over the generic GEMM bucket. ``module_chain`` is accepted
+    for signature compatibility but intentionally unused — matching on it would
+    mis-map a projection GEMM (launched from an attention module) to Attention."""
+    name = (kernel_name or "").lower()
+    for category in ("Attention", "MoE", "GEMM"):
+        if any(token in name for token in _CATEGORY_MATCHERS[category]):
+            return category
+    return None
+
+
+def summarize_projection(projection, tp: int, ridge: float | None) -> dict[str, dict]:
+    """Collapse a RooflineProjection into per-category roofline facts.
+
+    Sums FLOPs/bytes/roofline-time across the modeled ops of each category and
+    derives arithmetic intensity + a per-GPU roofline-time floor (the model
+    declares no TP plan for many custom archs, so FLOPs/bytes are whole-model;
+    dividing by ``tp`` approximates the per-GPU shard)."""
+    by_cat: dict[str, dict] = {}
+    for op in projection.ops:
+        if not op.modeled or op.category is None:
+            continue
+        acc = by_cat.setdefault(
+            op.category,
+            {
+                "flops": 0.0,
+                "bytes": 0.0,
+                "roofline_time_us": 0.0,
+                "bound_time": {},
+                # Per-invocation (one layer, one forward) FLOPs/bytes of the
+                # category's dominant op, used to scale against a trace kernel's
+                # measured per-invocation cost.
+                "flops_per_invocation": 0.0,
+                "bytes_per_invocation": 0.0,
+                "_dominant_flops": -1.0,
+            },
+        )
+        acc["flops"] += op.total_flops or 0.0
+        acc["bytes"] += op.total_bytes or 0.0
+        acc["roofline_time_us"] += op.total_roofline_time_us or 0.0
+        if op.roofline_bound:
+            acc["bound_time"][op.roofline_bound] = acc["bound_time"].get(
+                op.roofline_bound, 0.0
+            ) + (op.total_roofline_time_us or 0.0)
+        if (op.total_flops or 0.0) > acc["_dominant_flops"]:
+            acc["_dominant_flops"] = op.total_flops or 0.0
+            acc["flops_per_invocation"] = op.flops or 0.0
+            acc["bytes_per_invocation"] = op.bytes or 0.0
+    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
+    for cat, acc in by_cat.items():
+        ai = acc["flops"] / acc["bytes"] if acc["bytes"] else None
+        # The dominant-time bound classifies the category.
+        bound = (
+            max(acc["bound_time"], key=acc["bound_time"].get)
+            if acc["bound_time"]
+            else None
+        )
+        out[cat] = {
+            "bound": bound,
+            "arithmetic_intensity": ai,
+            "roofline_time_us": acc["roofline_time_us"],
+            "roofline_us_per_gpu": (
+                acc["roofline_time_us"] / tp if tp else acc["roofline_time_us"]
+            ),
+            "flops": acc["flops"],
+            "bytes": acc["bytes"],
+            "flops_per_invocation": acc["flops_per_invocation"],
+            "bytes_per_invocation": acc["bytes_per_invocation"],
+            "vs_ridge": (
+                None
+                if ai is None or ridge is None
+                else ("below" if ai < ridge else "above")
+            ),
+        }
+    return out
+
+
+def achieved_from_measurement(
+    facts: dict, time_ms: float | None, count: int | None, arch: dict | None
+) -> dict | None:
+    """Combine a kernel's measured time with the analytical per-invocation
+    FLOPs/bytes to report achieved throughput vs peak -- the measured side of a
+    roofline that the main report would compute from trace Input Dims.
+
+    Each of ``count`` invocations is assumed to run the projected per-invocation
+    (one-layer) shape. That holds for a single-regime capture; a mixed-regime
+    one (e.g. an agentic prefill+decode replay) will skew it, which the caller
+    must flag."""
+    if not time_ms or not count:
+        return None
+    fpi = facts.get("flops_per_invocation") or 0.0
+    bpi = facts.get("bytes_per_invocation") or 0.0
+    seconds = time_ms / 1000.0
+    achieved_tflops = (fpi * count) / seconds / 1e12 if fpi else None
+    achieved_gbps = (bpi * count) / seconds / 1e9 if bpi else None
+    peak_tflops = (arch or {}).get("peak_tflops")
+    mem_bw_gbps = (arch or {}).get("mem_bw_gbps")
+    # Report utilisation against whichever ceiling the roofline bound selects.
+    if facts.get("bound") == "MEMORY_BOUND":
+        pct_of_peak = (
+            100.0 * achieved_gbps / mem_bw_gbps
+            if achieved_gbps and mem_bw_gbps
+            else None
+        )
+        ceiling = "memory bandwidth"
+    else:
+        pct_of_peak = (
+            100.0 * achieved_tflops / peak_tflops
+            if achieved_tflops and peak_tflops
+            else None
+        )
+        ceiling = "compute peak"
+    return {
+        "achieved_tflops": achieved_tflops,
+        "achieved_gbps": achieved_gbps,
+        "pct_of_peak": pct_of_peak,
+        "ceiling": ceiling,
+    }
+
+
+def _dominant_ops(output_dir: Path) -> list[dict]:
+    """Every op across the orchestrator's per-category metrics, tagged with its
+    finding category, newest-first by GPU time."""
+    ops: list[dict] = []
+    for metrics_path in sorted(
+        glob.glob(str(output_dir / "category_data" / "*_metrics.json"))
+    ):
+        category = Path(metrics_path).name.removesuffix("_metrics.json")
+        try:
+            data = json.loads(Path(metrics_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
+            continue
+        for op in data.get("operations", []):
+            if isinstance(op, dict):
+                ops.append({**op, "_finding_category": category})
+    ops.sort(key=lambda o: o.get("time_ms") or 0.0, reverse=True)
+    return ops
+
+
+def _note(
+    kernel: str,
+    roofline_category: str,
+    facts: dict,
+    ridge: float | None,
+    achieved: dict | None,
+    regime: dict,
+) -> str:
+    ai = facts.get("arithmetic_intensity")
+    bound = (facts.get("bound") or "").replace("_", "-").lower() or "unclassified"
+    us = facts.get("roofline_us_per_gpu")
+    ridge_txt = f" vs the BF16 ridge of {ridge:.0f}" if ridge else ""
+    ai_txt = f"{ai:.1f} FLOP/byte{ridge_txt}" if ai is not None else "n/a"
+    us_txt = f"; ~{us/1000:.2f} ms/GPU roofline floor" if us else ""
+    phase = regime.get("phase") or "the captured"
+    achieved_txt = ""
+    if achieved and achieved.get("pct_of_peak") is not None:
+        thr = (
+            f"{achieved['achieved_gbps']:.0f} GB/s"
+            if achieved.get("ceiling") == "memory bandwidth"
+            and achieved.get("achieved_gbps")
+            else (
+                f"{achieved['achieved_tflops']:.1f} TFLOP/s"
+                if achieved.get("achieved_tflops")
+                else "n/a"
+            )
+        )
+        achieved_txt = (
+            f" Measured throughput ≈ {thr} = **{achieved['pct_of_peak']:.1f}% of "
+            f"{achieved['ceiling']}** (from the kernel's trace time against the "
+            f"config-derived FLOPs/bytes; assumes every invocation runs the "
+            f"projected {phase}-phase shape, so a mixed-regime capture skews it)."
+        )
+    return (
+        f"> **Analytical roofline (model-explorer, config-derived):** the trace "
+        f"carried no Input Dims for this kernel, so its shapes are taken from the "
+        f"model config and costed with the same PerfModel roofline used elsewhere. "
+        f"Modeled as **{roofline_category}**, it is **{bound}** at the {phase} regime "
+        f"(arithmetic intensity ≈ {ai_txt}{us_txt}).{achieved_txt}"
+    )
+
+
+def _is_modeled(op: dict) -> bool:
+    return (op.get("impact_estimate_method") or op.get("estimate_method")) == "modeled"
+
+
+def _kernel_name(op: dict) -> str:
+    return op.get("kernel_name") or op.get("name") or ""
+
+
+def _pick_dominant(ops: list[dict], categories: set[str]) -> dict[str, dict]:
+    """Highest-GPU-time unmodeled op per roofline category.
+
+    ``ops`` is already sorted by GPU time descending, so the first match wins.
+    Trace-modeled ops already carry a roofline and are skipped."""
+    picked: dict[str, dict] = {}
+    for op in ops:
+        if _is_modeled(op):
+            continue
+        category = classify_kernel(_kernel_name(op))
+        if category is None or category not in categories or category in picked:
+            continue
+        picked[category] = op
+    return picked
+
+
+def _phase_record(
+    op: dict, kernel: str, category: str, proj: dict, *, allow_achieved: bool
+) -> dict:
+    facts = proj["summary"][category]
+    regime = proj["regime"]
+    achieved = (
+        achieved_from_measurement(
+            facts, op.get("time_ms"), op.get("count"), proj.get("arch")
+        )
+        if allow_achieved
+        else None
+    )
+    return {
+        "phase": regime.get("phase"),
+        "batch_size": regime.get("batch_size"),
+        "seq_len": regime.get("seq_len"),
+        "bound": facts["bound"],
+        "arithmetic_intensity": facts["arithmetic_intensity"],
+        "roofline_us_per_gpu": facts["roofline_us_per_gpu"],
+        "flops": facts["flops"],
+        "bytes": facts["bytes"],
+        "measured_time_ms": op.get("time_ms"),
+        "measured_count": op.get("count"),
+        "achieved": achieved,
+        "note": _note(kernel, category, facts, proj.get("ridge"), achieved, regime),
+    }
+
+
+def _combined_note(category: str, phases: list[dict]) -> str:
+    """One blockquote covering every projected phase.
+
+    Achieved % is omitted: the kernel's measured time is not split by phase,
+    so scoring it against one phase's shapes would mis-state the result."""
+    bits = []
+    for phase in phases:
+        ai = phase.get("arithmetic_intensity")
+        bound = (phase.get("bound") or "").replace("_", "-").lower() or "unclassified"
+        us = phase.get("roofline_us_per_gpu")
+        ai_txt = f"{ai:.1f} FLOP/byte" if ai is not None else "n/a"
+        us_txt = f", ~{us / 1000:.2f} ms/GPU roofline floor" if us else ""
+        bits.append(
+            f"**{phase.get('phase') or 'phase'}** {bound} (AI ≈ {ai_txt}{us_txt})"
+        )
+    return (
+        "> **Analytical roofline (model-explorer, config-derived):** the trace "
+        "carried no Input Dims for this kernel, so its shapes are taken from the "
+        "model config and costed with the same PerfModel roofline used elsewhere. "
+        f"Modeled as **{category}** at each captured phase — {'; '.join(bits)}. "
+        "Measured time is not split by phase, so no achieved-% is reported."
+    )
+
+
+def _finalize_entry(acc: dict) -> dict:
+    phases = acc["phases"]
+    primary = phases[0]
+    multi = len(phases) > 1
+    return {
+        **acc,
+        "bound": primary["bound"],
+        "arithmetic_intensity": primary["arithmetic_intensity"],
+        "roofline_us_per_gpu": primary["roofline_us_per_gpu"],
+        "flops": primary["flops"],
+        "bytes": primary["bytes"],
+        "measured_time_ms": primary["measured_time_ms"],
+        "measured_count": primary["measured_count"],
+        "achieved": None if multi else primary.get("achieved"),
+        "note": (
+            _combined_note(acc["roofline_category"], phases)
+            if multi
+            else primary["note"]
+        ),
+    }
+
+
+def augment_phases(output_dir: Path, projections: list[dict]) -> dict:
+    """Attach roofline facts for one or more projected regimes.
+
+    Each item of ``projections`` is ``{summary, regime, ridge, arch}``. Only the
+    highest-GPU-time unmodeled kernel per roofline category is augmented.
+
+    When the metrics ops carry a ``phase``, each regime is matched to the ops of
+    that phase and the achieved % uses that phase's measured time. When they do
+    not, every regime is attached to the same dominant kernel and the achieved %
+    is reported only for a single regime — a mixed capture's measured time is
+    not split by phase."""
+    ops = _dominant_ops(output_dir)
+    phased = any(op.get("phase") not in (None, "") for op in ops)
+    grouped: dict[str, dict] = {}
+
+    def add(op: dict, proj: dict, *, allow_achieved: bool) -> None:
+        category = classify_kernel(_kernel_name(op))
+        if category is None or category not in proj["summary"]:
+            return
+        kernel = _kernel_name(op)
+        record = _phase_record(
+            op, kernel, category, proj, allow_achieved=allow_achieved
+        )
+        acc = grouped.setdefault(
+            kernel,
+            {
+                "kernel": kernel,
+                "finding_category": op.get("_finding_category"),
+                "roofline_category": category,
+                "phases": [],
+            },
+        )
+        if any(existing.get("phase") == record["phase"] for existing in acc["phases"]):
+            return
+        acc["phases"].append(record)
+
+    if phased:
+        for proj in projections:
+            phase_name = str(proj["regime"].get("phase") or "").lower()
+            phase_ops = [
+                op for op in ops if str(op.get("phase") or "").lower() == phase_name
+            ]
+            for op in _pick_dominant(phase_ops, set(proj["summary"])).values():
+                add(op, proj, allow_achieved=True)
+    else:
+        categories: set[str] = set()
+        for proj in projections:
+            categories |= set(proj["summary"])
+        picked = _pick_dominant(ops, categories)
+        for category, op in picked.items():
+            covering = [proj for proj in projections if category in proj["summary"]]
+            # Achieved % divides one measured time by one phase's FLOPs/bytes.
+            # A kernel scored at two phases has no per-phase measured time.
+            for proj in covering:
+                add(op, proj, allow_achieved=len(covering) == 1)
+
+    entries = [_finalize_entry(acc) for acc in grouped.values()]
+    single = len(projections) == 1
+    payload = {
+        "regime": projections[0]["regime"] if single else None,
+        "regimes": [proj["regime"] for proj in projections],
+        "ridge_flops_per_byte": projections[0].get("ridge") if single else None,
+        "roofline_by_category": (
+            projections[0]["summary"]
+            if single
+            else [proj["summary"] for proj in projections]
+        ),
+        "entries": entries,
+    }
+    meta = output_dir / "metadata"
+    meta.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    (meta / "roofline_augmentation.json").write_text(
+        json.dumps(payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8"
+    )
+    payload["merged_findings"] = merge_into_priority_data(output_dir, entries)
+    return payload
+
+
+def augment(
+    output_dir: Path,
+    summary: dict[str, dict],
+    regime: dict,
+    ridge: float | None,
+    arch: dict | None = None,
+) -> dict:
+    """Attach one regime's roofline facts to the dominant unmodeled kernel of
+    each roofline category. See :func:`augment_phases`."""
+    return augment_phases(
+        output_dir,
+        [{"summary": summary, "regime": regime, "ridge": ridge, "arch": arch}],
+    )
+
+
+def _roofline_block(entry: dict, phase: dict | None = None) -> dict:
+    """An additive finding block. ``phase`` selects one regime of a multi-phase
+    entry; otherwise the entry's own (possibly combined) note is used."""
+    source = phase or entry
+    block = {
+        "source": "analytical-model-explorer",
+        "roofline_category": entry["roofline_category"],
+        "bound": source["bound"],
+        "arithmetic_intensity": source["arithmetic_intensity"],
+        "roofline_us_per_gpu": source["roofline_us_per_gpu"],
+        "achieved": source.get("achieved"),
+        "note": source["note"],
+    }
+    if phase is not None and phase.get("phase"):
+        block["phase"] = phase["phase"]
+    elif len(entry.get("phases") or []) > 1:
+        block["phases"] = [
+            {
+                "phase": item.get("phase"),
+                "bound": item["bound"],
+                "arithmetic_intensity": item["arithmetic_intensity"],
+                "roofline_us_per_gpu": item["roofline_us_per_gpu"],
+                "achieved": item.get("achieved"),
+            }
+            for item in entry["phases"]
+        ]
+    return block
+
+
+def merge_into_priority_data(output_dir: Path, entries: list[dict]) -> int:
+    """Fold each roofline entry into the matching ``priority_data.json`` finding.
+
+    Matches an entry to a finding by its kernel name appearing in a member's
+    ``operation`` string. A finding that carries a ``phase`` receives only the
+    matching phase; a finding with no phase receives the combined note. The
+    merge attaches an additive ``roofline`` block and leaves every existing
+    field untouched -- in particular ``bound_type``, ``efficiency_pct`` and
+    ``estimate_method``. Report generation renders ``findings[i].roofline.note``
+    verbatim. Returns the number of findings annotated."""
+    path = output_dir / "priority_data.json"
+    if not path.is_file() or not entries:
+        return 0
+    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    findings = data.get("findings", [])
+    merged = 0
+    for entry in entries:
+        kernel = entry["kernel"]
+        phases = entry.get("phases") or []
+        for finding in findings:
+            if "roofline" in finding:
+                continue
+            members = finding.get("members") or []
+            if not any(
+                kernel in str(member.get("operation", "")) for member in members
+            ):
+                continue
+            finding_phase = finding.get("phase")
+            if finding_phase and phases:
+                match = next(
+                    (
+                        phase
+                        for phase in phases
+                        if str(phase.get("phase") or "").lower()
+                        == str(finding_phase).lower()
+                    ),
+                    None,
+                )
+                if match is None:
+                    continue
+                finding["roofline"] = _roofline_block(entry, match)
+            else:
+                finding["roofline"] = _roofline_block(entry)
+            merged += 1
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
+    return merged
+
+
+def report_notes(output_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """``{kernel_name: markdown_note}`` for report generation to inject beside
+    each kernel in the Detailed Analysis. Empty if augmentation was not run."""
+    path = Path(output_dir) / "metadata" / "roofline_augmentation.json"
+    if not path.is_file():
+        return {}
+    payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    return {e["kernel"]: e["note"] for e in payload.get("entries", [])}
+
+
+def _ridge(gpu_arch: dict | None) -> float | None:
+    if not gpu_arch:
+        return None
+    peak = (gpu_arch.get("max_achievable_tflops") or {}).get("matrix_bf16")
+    bw = gpu_arch.get("mem_bw_gbps")
+    if not peak or not bw:
+        return None
+    return peak * 1e12 / (bw * 1e9)
+
+
+_PHASES = ("prefill", "decode")
+
+
+def phase_argvs(spec: dict) -> list[list[str]]:
+    """One roofline-CLI argv per phase in a ``roofline_augment_args`` spec.
+
+    Returns an empty list when ``source`` is missing or ``phases`` is empty:
+    the caller skips. Raises ``ValueError`` or ``TypeError`` when a present spec
+    is invalid.
+    """
+    source = spec.get("source")
+    phases = spec.get("phases") or []
+    if not source or not phases:
+        return []
+    if not isinstance(phases, list):
+        raise TypeError("phases must be a list")
+    base = [str(source)]
+    if spec.get("code_path"):
+        base += ["--code-path", str(spec["code_path"])]
+    if spec.get("engine"):
+        base += ["--engine", str(spec["engine"])]
+    for key, flag in (("tp", "--tp"), ("pp", "--pp"), ("ep", "--ep")):
+        if spec.get(key) is not None:
+            base += [flag, str(int(spec[key]))]
+    if spec.get("gpu_arch_name"):
+        base += ["--gpu-arch-name", str(spec["gpu_arch_name"])]
+    if spec.get("gpu_arch_json_path"):
+        base += ["--gpu-arch-json-path", str(spec["gpu_arch_json_path"])]
+    argvs = []
+    for phase in phases:
+        if not isinstance(phase, dict):
+            raise TypeError("each phase must be an object")
+        name = str(phase.get("phase") or "")
+        if name not in _PHASES:
+            raise ValueError(f"phase must be prefill or decode, got {name!r}")
+        try:
+            batch = int(phase["batch_size"])
+            seq = int(phase["seq_len"])
+        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"phase {name} needs integer batch_size and seq_len"
+            ) from exc
+        argv = base + [
+            "--phase",
+            name,
+            "--batch-size",
+            str(batch),
+            "--seq-len",
+            str(seq),
+        ]
+        dims = phase.get("dims") or {}
+        if not isinstance(dims, dict):
+            raise TypeError("phase dims must be an object")
+        for key, value in dims.items():
+            argv += ["--dim", f"{key}={int(value)}"]
+        argvs.append(argv)
+    return argvs
+
+
+def _projection_record(proj_args, projection, gpu_arch) -> dict:
+    ridge = _ridge(gpu_arch)
+    return {
+        "summary": summarize_projection(projection, proj_args.tp, ridge),
+        "regime": {
+            "phase": proj_args.phase,
+            "batch_size": proj_args.batch_size,
+            "seq_len": proj_args.seq_len,
+            "dims": dict(item.split("=", 1) for item in (proj_args.dim or [])),
+            "tp": proj_args.tp,
+            "pp": proj_args.pp,
+            "ep": proj_args.ep,
+            "engine": proj_args.engine,
+        },
+        "ridge": ridge,
+        "arch": {
+            "peak_tflops": (
+                (gpu_arch.get("max_achievable_tflops") or {}).get("matrix_bf16")
+                if gpu_arch
+                else None
+            ),
+            "mem_bw_gbps": gpu_arch.get("mem_bw_gbps") if gpu_arch else None,
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def _report(output_dir: Path, payload: dict) -> None:
+    categories = payload.get("roofline_by_category")
+    n_categories = len(categories) if isinstance(categories, dict) else 0
+    if not n_categories:
+        n_categories = len({e["roofline_category"] for e in payload["entries"]})
+    print(
+        f"Wrote {output_dir / 'metadata' / 'roofline_augmentation.json'}: "
+        f"{len(payload['entries'])} kernel(s) augmented across "
+        f"{n_categories} roofline categor(ies)."
+    )
+    for entry in payload["entries"]:
+        ai = entry["arithmetic_intensity"]
+        print(
+            f"  {entry['kernel']}: {entry['roofline_category']} {entry['bound']} "
+            f"AI={ai:.1f} FLOP/byte  "
+            f"~{(entry['roofline_us_per_gpu'] or 0) / 1000:.2f} ms/GPU"
+            if ai is not None
+            else f"  {entry['kernel']}: {entry['roofline_category']} {entry['bound']}"
+        )
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    # Import here so the heavy Visualizer extra is only needed when augmenting.
+    from TraceLens.Visualizer.model_explorer_export.roofline_cli import (
+        build_parser,
+        run_projection,
+    )
+
+    pre = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
+    pre.add_argument(
+        "--output-dir",
+        required=True,
+        help="Orchestrator output directory (holds category_data/, metadata/).",
+    )
+    pre.add_argument(
+        "--args-json",
+        type=Path,
+        help=(
+            "roofline_augment_args.json written by the roofline-augment sub-agent. "
+            "Projects every phase in the file. Skips when source or phases is empty."
+        ),
+    )
+    ns, rest = pre.parse_known_args(argv)
+    if ns.args_json and rest:
+        print(
+            "roofline_augment: pass --args-json or projection flags, not both",
+            file=sys.stderr,
+        )
+        return 1
+
+    if ns.args_json:
+        try:
+            spec = json.loads(ns.args_json.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+            if not isinstance(spec, dict):
+                raise TypeError("roofline_augment_args.json must be an object")
+            argvs = phase_argvs(spec)
+        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
+            print(f"roofline_augment: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 1
+        if not argvs:
+            reason = spec.get("skipped") or "source or phases unresolved"
+            print(f"roofline_augment: skipped ({reason})")
+            return 0
+        cli_argvs = argvs
+    else:
+        # The remaining args are the model-source + runtime-regime flags shared
+        # with the roofline-projection CLI (checkpoint, --engine, --tp, --phase, ...).
+        cli_argvs = [rest]
+
+    projections = []
+    for cli_argv in cli_argvs:
+        proj_args = build_parser().parse_args(cli_argv)
+        try:
+            projection, gpu_arch, layout_warnings = run_projection(proj_args)
+        except (ValueError, KeyError, RuntimeError) as exc:
+            print(f"roofline_augment: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 1
+        for text in layout_warnings:
+            print(f"Warning: {text}", file=sys.stderr)
+        projections.append(_projection_record(proj_args, projection, gpu_arch))
+
+    output_dir = Path(ns.output_dir)
+    payload = augment_phases(output_dir, projections)
+    _report(output_dir, payload)
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+###############################################################################
+# Copyright (c) 2026 Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. All rights reserved.
+#
+# See LICENSE for license information.
+###############################################################################
+
+"""CLI for a static, trace-free full-model roofline projection.
+
+Loads a checkpoint through the same AST backend as the Model Explorer export
+(``TraceLens.ModelUtils`` loader), stops expansion at ops with a direct
+``TraceLens.PerfModel`` formula, and prints a kernel-by-kernel roofline table
+plus a model-level rollup -- no trace or GPU run required.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import csv
+import json
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from TraceLens.Agent.Analysis.utils.arch_utils import list_platforms, load_arch
+from TraceLens.ModelUtils.cli_common import (
+    add_engine_argument,
+    add_model_source_arguments,
+    add_runtime_regime_arguments,
+    load_architecture_spec_from_args,
+)
+from TraceLens.ModelUtils.loader import resolve_checkpoint_arg
+from TraceLens.ModelUtils.parallel_plan import ParallelDegree, build_parallel_layout
+from TraceLens.Visualizer.model_explorer_export.roofline_projection import (
+    _CONV_COMPUTATIONS,
+    RooflineOp,
+    conv_ops_from_meta,
+    project_roofline,
+)
+
+# Constants
+
+_TABLE_COLUMNS = (
+    "section",
+    "name",
+    "category",
+    "instances",
+    "total_flops",
+    "total_bytes",
+    "compute_spec",
+    "roofline_bound",
+    "total_roofline_time_us",
+    "reason",
+)
+
+
+def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        prog="TraceLens_model_roofline_projection",
+        description=(
+            "Project a kernel-by-kernel roofline for a model checkpoint from its "
+            "config and modeling source alone, with no trace or GPU run. Ops are "
+            "costed with TraceLens.PerfModel's analytical FLOPs/bytes formulas; "
+            "ops with no direct formula (embeddings, MoE routing, convolutions, "
+            "...) are reported as unmodeled rather than silently dropped."
+        ),
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "source",
+        nargs="?",
+        help="Hugging Face model id or local checkpoint directory (alias for --checkpoint)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--checkpoint",
+        "-c",
+        help="Hugging Face model id or local checkpoint path for config.json",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--title",
+        help="Architecture display name override",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--batch-size",
+        type=int,
+        default=1,
+        metavar="N",
+        help="Batch size to project at (default: 1)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--seq-len",
+        type=int,
+        default=2048,
+        metavar="N",
+        help="Sequence length to project at (default: 2048)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--dim",
+        action="append",
+        default=[],
+        metavar="KEY=VALUE",
+        help=(
+            "Override one symbolic shape dimension with a concrete int, "
+            "repeatable (e.g. --dim past_len=1024). Takes precedence over "
+            "--batch-size/--seq-len for the same key."
+        ),
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--gpu-arch-name",
+        metavar="NAME",
+        help=(
+            "Named GPU architecture spec to bound against "
+            f"(available: {', '.join(list_platforms())}). Without this or "
+            "--gpu-arch-json-path, FLOPs/bytes are still reported but no "
+            "roofline time/bound is computed."
+        ),
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--gpu-arch-json-path",
+        type=Path,
+        metavar="PATH",
+        help="Path to a GPU arch JSON (same schema as --gpu-arch-name); takes precedence",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output-csv",
+        type=Path,
+        metavar="PATH",
+        help="Write the per-op table as CSV",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output-json",
+        type=Path,
+        metavar="PATH",
+        help="Write the per-op table and rollup as JSON",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--top-n",
+        type=int,
+        default=20,
+        metavar="N",
+        help="Rows to print to stdout, ranked by total roofline time (default: 20; 0 for all)",
+    )
+    add_model_source_arguments(parser)
+    add_runtime_regime_arguments(parser)
+
+    partition_group = parser.add_argument_group(
+        "device partitions",
+        "How many ways to split the model before projecting its roofline. The "
+        "split itself comes from the plans on its Hugging Face config "
+        "(base_model_tp_plan, base_model_pp_plan, base_model_ep_plan, plus the "
+        "causal-LM head), or, with --engine, from that inference engine's own "
+        "parallel-layer classes. 1 leaves that axis unsplit; the projection then "
+        "covers one GPU's own share of the work, the same per-GPU shapes the "
+        "Model Explorer viewer would draw for this split.",
+    )
+    add_engine_argument(parser, group=partition_group)
+    partition_group.add_argument(
+        "--tp",
+        type=int,
+        default=1,
+        metavar="N",
+        help="Tensor-parallel partitions (default: 1).",
+    )
+    partition_group.add_argument(
+        "--pp",
+        type=int,
+        default=1,
+        metavar="N",
+        help="Pipeline-parallel partitions (default: 1).",
+    )
+    partition_group.add_argument(
+        "--ep",
+        type=int,
+        default=1,
+        metavar="N",
+        help="Expert-parallel partitions (default: 1).",
+    )
+    return parser
+
+
+def parse_dim_overrides(entries: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]:
+    """Parse ``--dim KEY=VALUE`` pairs into an int-valued dict."""
+    overrides: dict[str, int] = {}
+    for entry in entries:
+        key, sep, value = entry.partition("=")
+        if not sep or not key.strip():
+            raise ValueError(f"--dim must be KEY=VALUE, got {entry!r}")
+        try:
+            overrides[key.strip()] = int(value.strip())
+        except ValueError as exc:
+            raise ValueError(f"--dim value must be an int, got {entry!r}") from exc
+    return overrides
+
+
+def _op_row(op: RooflineOp) -> dict[str, object]:
+    return {
+        "section": op.section,
+        "name": op.name,
+        "computation": op.computation,
+        "category": op.category,
+        "instances": op.instances,
+        "flops": op.flops,
+        "bytes": op.bytes,
+        "total_flops": op.total_flops,
+        "total_bytes": op.total_bytes,
+        "compute_spec": op.compute_spec,
+        "roofline_bound": op.roofline_bound,
+        "roofline_time_us": op.roofline_time_us,
+        "total_roofline_time_us": op.total_roofline_time_us,
+        "reason": op.reason,
+    }
+
+
+def format_table(ops: list[RooflineOp], *, top_n: int) -> str:
+    """Render a fixed-width table of *ops*, ranked by total roofline time."""
+    ranked = sorted(ops, key=lambda op: op.total_roofline_time_us or 0, reverse=True)
+    if top_n > 0:
+        ranked = ranked[:top_n]
+    rows = [_op_row(op) for op in ranked]
+    widths = {
+        col: (
+            max(len(col), *(len(_format_cell(row[col])) for row in rows))
+            if rows
+            else len(col)
+        )
+        for col in _TABLE_COLUMNS
+    }
+    lines = [" | ".join(col.ljust(widths[col]) for col in _TABLE_COLUMNS)]
+    lines.append("-+-".join("-" * widths[col] for col in _TABLE_COLUMNS))
+    for row in rows:
+        lines.append(
+            " | ".join(
+                _format_cell(row[col]).ljust(widths[col]) for col in _TABLE_COLUMNS
+            )
+        )
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+def _format_cell(value: object) -> str:
+    if value is None:
+        return "-"
+    if isinstance(value, float):
+        return f"{value:,.1f}"
+    return str(value)
+
+
+def write_csv(ops: list[RooflineOp], path: Path) -> None:
+    rows = [_op_row(op) for op in ops]
+    fieldnames = list(rows[0].keys()) if rows else []
+    with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=fieldnames)
+        writer.writeheader()
+        writer.writerows(rows)
+
+
+def run_projection(args):
+    """Resolve the model and project its roofline from parsed CLI ``args``.
+
+    Shared by the ``TraceLens_model_roofline_projection`` CLI and the
+    orchestrator roofline-augmentation utility (``roofline_augment``). Raises
+    ``ValueError`` for an invalid model source or ``--dim`` override, ``KeyError``
+    for an unknown ``--gpu-arch-name``, and ``RuntimeError`` when the architecture
+    fails to load. Returns ``(projection, gpu_arch, layout_warnings)``.
+    """
+    checkpoint = resolve_checkpoint_arg(checkpoint=args.checkpoint, source=args.source)
+    if checkpoint is None and args.github is None:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Provide a Hugging Face checkpoint (SOURCE or --checkpoint) and/or --github"
+        )
+    extra_dims = parse_dim_overrides(args.dim)
+    gpu_arch = None
+    if args.gpu_arch_json_path is not None:
+        gpu_arch = json.loads(args.gpu_arch_json_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    elif args.gpu_arch_name is not None:
+        gpu_arch = load_arch(args.gpu_arch_name)
+    try:
+        spec = load_architecture_spec_from_args(
+            checkpoint, args, title=args.title, stop_at_roofline_ops=True
+        )
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Error loading architecture: {exc}") from exc
+    degree = ParallelDegree(tp=args.tp, pp=args.pp, ep=args.ep)
+    layout_warnings: list[str] = []
+    if degree.requested():
+        spec.parallel_layout = build_parallel_layout(spec, degree)
+        for line in spec.parallel_layout.fact_lines():
+            text = line.strip()
+            if (
+                "does not divide" in text
+                or text.startswith("The model declares")
+                or text.startswith("No Hugging Face")
+            ):
+                layout_warnings.append(text)
+    projection = project_roofline(
+        spec,
+        batch_size=args.batch_size,
+        seq_len=args.seq_len,
+        extra_dims=extra_dims,
+        gpu_arch=gpu_arch,
+        checkpoint=checkpoint,
+    )
+    # Convolutional models: the graph draws one conv per stage (and the stem /
+    # downsampling convs that lead those stages). Cost each live instance from a
+    # meta-device forward and let it supersede the graph's conv rows so a
+    # repeated stage is not counted twice.
+    if checkpoint is not None:
+        from TraceLens.ModelUtils.meta_trace import trace_meta_conv_ops
+
+        conv_ops = conv_ops_from_meta(
+            trace_meta_conv_ops(checkpoint, batch_size=args.batch_size),
+            dtype=str((spec.raw_config or {}).get("torch_dtype") or "bfloat16"),
+            gpu_arch=gpu_arch,
+        )
+        if conv_ops:
+            projection.ops = [
+                op for op in projection.ops if op.computation not in _CONV_COMPUTATIONS
+            ] + conv_ops
+    return projection, gpu_arch, layout_warnings
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = build_parser()
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+
+    try:
+        projection, gpu_arch, layout_warnings = run_projection(args)
+    except ValueError as exc:
+        parser.error(str(exc))
+    except KeyError:
+        parser.error(
+            f"Unknown --gpu-arch-name {args.gpu_arch_name!r}; "
+            f"available: {', '.join(list_platforms())}"
+        )
+    except RuntimeError as exc:
+        print(str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    for text in layout_warnings:
+        print(f"Warning: {text}", file=sys.stderr)
+
+    print(format_table(projection.ops, top_n=args.top_n))
+    print()
+    totals = projection.totals()
+    print(
+        f"Total: {totals['total_flops']:,.0f} FLOPs, {totals['total_bytes']:,.0f} bytes, "
+        f"modeled {totals['modeled_op_count']} ops / unmodeled {totals['unmodeled_op_count']} ops "
+        f"({(totals['modeled_output_element_share'] or 0) * 100:.1f}% of output elements modeled)"
+    )
+    if totals["total_roofline_time_us"]:
+        print(
+            f"Roofline time: {totals['total_roofline_time_us']:,.1f} us "
+            f"(compute-bound {totals['compute_bound_time_us']:,.1f} us, "
+            f"memory-bound {totals['memory_bound_time_us']:,.1f} us)"
+        )
+    elif gpu_arch is None:
+        print(
+            "No --gpu-arch-name/--gpu-arch-json-path given: FLOPs/bytes only, no roofline time."
+        )
+
+    if args.output_csv is not None:
+        write_csv(projection.ops, args.output_csv)
+        print(f"Wrote CSV: {args.output_csv}")
+    if args.output_json is not None:
+        payload = {"ops": [_op_row(op) for op in projection.ops], "totals": totals}
+        args.output_json.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
+        print(f"Wrote JSON: {args.output_json}")
+
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+Walks the same merged Model Explorer graph the visualizer draws (see
+:func:`TraceLens.Visualizer.model_explorer_export.ast_build.build_model_explorer_payload`),
+stopped at ops with a direct :mod:`TraceLens.PerfModel.perf_model` formula (see
+:func:`TraceLens.ModelUtils.build_roofline_basic_ops`), and costs each leaf with
+PerfModel's analytical FLOPs/bytes. Reusing the graph rather than a separate
+operator export means a ``--tp``/``--pp``/``--ep`` split, and the merged
+per-GPU local shapes it produces, is the same split and the same shapes the
+visualizer draws -- not a second, independently-matched approximation of it.
+
+Op coverage is intentionally narrow: GEMM (``Linear``/``matmul``/``bmm``), CONV,
+SDPA, the Normalization family, Softmax, generic elementwise/reduction ops, and
+MoE expert routing -- exactly the leaf granularity
+:func:`TraceLens.ModelUtils.build_roofline_basic_ops` stops AST expansion at,
+plus the vLLM/SGLang engine boundaries (``ParallelLMHead``, ``FusedMoEFactory``)
+that never expand at all (see "Known approximations" below). Convolutions in a
+graph node are costed only when the meta-device pass threaded the kernel
+geometry onto the node's ``details`` attr (``conv_weight=[...]``); the
+input/output shapes alone cannot recover the weight's kernel size or groups.
+Anything else (embeddings, a conv with no threaded geometry) is reported as
+"unmodeled" rather than silently dropped, so the projection's coverage is always
+visible instead of assumed.
+
+Convolutional models are handled separately. The graph expands a non-uniform
+stage once (one conv node per stage, plus the stem and each stage's leading
+downsampling conv). :func:`conv_ops_from_meta` still costs every live conv
+instance a meta-device forward captures (see
+:func:`TraceLens.ModelUtils.meta_trace.trace_meta_conv_ops`) -- each already
+carries the concrete ``[B, C, H, W]`` shapes and weight geometry CONV needs --
+and the CLI lets those supersede the graph's conv rows so a repeated stage is
+not counted twice.
+
+Known approximations, stated once here rather than scattered in comments:
+  - GEMM bias is assumed absent (bias FLOPs are O(M*N), negligible next to the
+    O(M*N*K) matmul term for any realistic K).
+  - Every Normalization op is assumed affine; RMSNorm is assumed bias-free,
+    every other norm is assumed to have a bias.
+  - SDPA is assumed causal exactly when the query and key/value sequence
+    lengths resolve equal (self-attention prefill shape), non-causal otherwise.
+  - An op's instance count is the innermost ``"<N>x_..."`` repeat-count
+    namespace segment surrounding it (the merged graph's own per-variant tile
+    count), or 1 for an op outside any repeated layer. A hybrid/variant layer
+    mix (sliding-window vs. global attention, MoE inserted only every few
+    layers, ...) is therefore attributed per-variant already, unlike a flat
+    ``num_hidden_layers`` scale-up.
+  - ``ParallelLMHead``/``FusedMoEFactory`` (vLLM/SGLang) are read from the
+    engine's own source, not the model's, and shape_inference has no rule for
+    either -- their exported shape is an unresolved pass-through, not a real
+    one. Both are costed from the architecture's own dims (batch, seq, vocab,
+    hidden, experts-per-token, expert intermediate size) instead, the same
+    numbers the model's own config declares, rather than from their (unusable)
+    node shape.
+  - MoE routing is costed as ``experts_per_tok`` grouped-GEMM passes per token
+    (the gate_up_proj and down_proj of only the SELECTED experts), never
+    ``num_experts`` passes -- the router picks a subset per token, so costing
+    every expert for every token would overstate FLOPs by
+    ``num_experts / experts_per_tok``. The expert GEMMs use :class:`GroupedGemm`
+    over ``G = min(num_experts, active_tokens)`` distinct weight matrices, so the
+    weight-byte term reflects the experts actually streamed (``G`` falls back to
+    1, the prior single-weight cost, when ``num_experts`` is unknown). When
+    expert-parallel (``--ep > 1``) the dispatch/combine all-to-all that moves
+    token hidden states between EP ranks is added as FLOPs-free data movement
+    (:class:`MoEComm`). The router's own softmax/top-k selection and the
+    shared-expert add are not separately costed (both are O(tokens), negligible
+    next to the O(tokens*hidden*intermediate) expert GEMMs).
+"""
+

+# meta-device pass (``conv_weight=[...]``, ``conv_bias=0|1``, ``conv_transposed=0|1``)

+# GEMM formula applies once the label is recognized as one -- except
+# ``ParallelLMHead``, read from the engine's own source where shape_inference

+_ENGINE_LINEAR_CLASS_MARKERS = ("ParallelLinear", "ParallelLMHead", "ReplicatedLinear")
+_ENGINE_HEAD_CLASS_MARKERS = ("ParallelLMHead",)
+# vLLM's ``FusedMoEFactory`` (SGLang's own MoE factory is a differently-named

+# expert-GEMM + combine pipeline across several more files; expanding it would
+# trade today's one labeled boundary for a deep, mostly quantization/EPLB-
+# plumbing subgraph with no clearer a picture of the actual compute. It stays

+_ENGINE_MOE_CLASS_MARKERS = ("FusedMoE",)
+
+# Normalization family, keyed by a case-insensitive substring of the exported
+# computation label: (kind, has_bias, channel_first). Matched by substring
+# rather than exact class name because real checkpoints almost always subclass

+# no learned bias; every other family here is assumed to have one. "generic"
+# families share the base Normalization.flops_func/bytes_func; "rmsnorm" uses
+# RMSNorm's own flops()/bytes() (see _rmsnorm_flops/_rmsnorm_bytes -- RMSNorm
+# has no flops_func/bytes_func to call directly). channel_first classes
+# normalize over axis 1 (conv-style [N, C, ...]); the rest normalize over the
+# trailing feature axis.
+_NORMALIZATION_FAMILIES: tuple[tuple[str, str, bool, bool], ...] = (
+    ("rmsnorm", "rmsnorm", False, False),
+    ("layernorm", "generic", True, False),
+    ("groupnorm", "generic", True, True),
+    ("instancenorm", "generic", True, True),
+    ("batchnorm", "generic", True, True),

+def _classify_normalization(computation: str) -> tuple[str, bool, bool] | None:
+    """Map a (possibly model-specific subclass) norm label to its formula family."""
+    lowered = computation.lower()
+    for needle, kind, has_bias, channel_first in _NORMALIZATION_FAMILIES:
+        if needle in lowered:
+            return kind, has_bias, channel_first
+    return None

+# A node's instance count is the innermost repeat-count namespace segment

+# the count is the digits before ``x_``.
+_REPEAT_NAMESPACE_SEGMENT = re.compile(r"^(?:s\d+_)?(\d+)x(?:_|$)")

+# Ids this synthetic/boundary-marker prefix never carries real computation --
+# an @input/@output port marker or a collective TraceLens inserted for a

+_NON_COMPUTE_ID_MARKER = "@comm:"
